title: 折钵山升旗
source: 《硫磺岛升旗》（Raising the Flag on Iwo Jima），美联社摄影记者乔·罗森塔尔摄于1945年2月23日上午10时30分前后，硫磺岛折钵山山顶。画面要点：低机位仰视，六名陆战队员在黑色火山岩渣坡上合力竖起旗杆，旗杆自右下斜向左上，顶端48星美国国旗迎风展开，背景是阴天大面积浅灰天空，左下远景隐约可见山麓与海岸。
story: 1945年2月19日，美军在东京以南约1200公里的硫磺岛登陆。2月23日上午10时20分左右，战役第五天，海军陆战队第五师第28团E连的巡逻队攻上岛南端高169米的死火山折钵山山顶，把一面小国旗绑上从山顶捡到的日式集水管升了起来。旗帜太小，山下苦战的官兵与海面上的舰船几乎看不见，营部随即命人从山脚的坦克登陆舰LST-779取来一面更大的星条旗。第二次升旗被随军的美联社摄影记者乔·罗森塔尔赶上：他背着一台Speed Graphic新闻相机爬上山脊时，六名陆战队员正在合力竖起粗大的金属旗杆，他转过身，在几乎来不及细看取景器的瞬间按下了快门。硫磺岛上空昏沉的云、黑色的火山岩渣与那面骤然展开的国旗，就此定格成二十世纪最著名的新闻照片之一。

照片中六名合力扶旗的士兵全部是海军陆战队员，但他们的名字曾长期被搞错：最初广为流传的名单把医护兵约翰·布拉德利与队员雷内·加尼翁写进了照片，海军陆战队于2016年6月确认对应位置实为哈罗德·舒尔茨，2019年10月又确认另一处实为哈罗德·凯勒。最终认定的六人是：迈克尔·斯特兰克、哈伦·布洛克、富兰克林·索斯利、艾拉·海斯、哈罗德·舒尔茨与哈罗德·凯勒。胜利的一刻没能延续太久——斯特兰克与布洛克于3月1日、索斯利于3月21日相继阵亡在这座岛上；用电影摄影机拍下升旗过程的陆战队摄影员比尔·热诺斯特也在3月4日战死，他所拍的影片至今下落不明。

罗森塔尔的照片在拍摄当年即获普利策摄影奖，是迄今唯一一张在拍摄同年获奖的新闻照片；它登上全美报纸头版，被制成邮票与海报，1954年以其为原型的海军陆战队战争纪念碑在弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿落成。硫磺岛战役一直打到3月26日：美军付出约6800人阵亡、两万余人负伤的代价，约两万余名日本守军几乎全部战死。对经历过那场战争的一代人来说，折钵山顶升起的那面旗，是苦战中最先抵达的胜利消息，也是整场战争代价与意志的缩影。

en.title: Raising the Flag on Iwo Jima
en.source: Raising the Flag on Iwo Jima, taken by AP war photographer Joe Rosenthal at about 10:30 on the morning of February 23, 1945, on the summit of Mount Suribachi, Iwo Jima.
en.points: Shot from a low angle looking up: six Marines heave a flagpole upright together on a slope of black volcanic cinders, the pole running diagonally from lower right to upper left, a 48-star American flag unfurling in the wind at its top. A broad expanse of pale gray overcast sky fills the background, with the foothills and the coastline faintly visible in the lower-left distance.
story: On February 19, 1945, American forces landed on Iwo Jima, an island some 1,200 kilometers south of Tokyo. At about 10:20 on the morning of February 23, the fifth day of the battle, a patrol of Company E, 28th Marine Regiment, 5th Marine Division, fought its way onto the summit of Mount Suribachi, the 169-meter extinct volcano at the island's southern end, and raised a small national flag lashed to a piece of Japanese drainpipe found on the summit. The flag was too small: the men fighting below and the ships offshore could hardly see it, and battalion headquarters at once sent for a larger Stars and Stripes from LST-779, a tank landing ship lying at the foot of the mountain. The second raising was the one AP war photographer Joe Rosenthal happened upon: climbing the ridge under a Speed Graphic press camera, he came up as six Marines were heaving the heavy metal pole upright together; he turned, and with barely time to look through the viewfinder, tripped the shutter. The sullen clouds over Iwo Jima, the black volcanic cinders, and the flag suddenly spread against them were fixed for good as one of the most famous news photographs of the twentieth century.

All six men heaving at the flagpole were Marines, yet their names were for long wrongly given: the list first in wide circulation included Navy corpsman John Bradley and Marine Rene Gagnon, until in June 2016 the Marine Corps confirmed that one of the positions was in fact Harold Schultz, and in October 2019 that another was Harold Keller. The six finally identified are Michael Strank, Harlon Block, Franklin Sousley, Ira Hayes, Harold Schultz, and Harold Keller. The moment of victory lasted little: Strank and Block were killed on the island on March 1, Sousley on March 21; Bill Genaust, the Marine motion-picture photographer who filmed the raising, fell on March 4, and the film he shot has never been found.

Rosenthal's photograph won the Pulitzer Prize for Photography the same year it was taken—the only news photograph to win the award in its year of exposure. It filled the front pages of America's newspapers, became a stamp and a poster, and in 1954 the Marine Corps War Memorial modeled upon it was dedicated at Arlington, Virginia. The battle of Iwo Jima ground on until March 26: the United States paid about 6,800 dead and more than 20,000 wounded, while the roughly 20,000 Japanese defenders fell almost to the last man. For the generation that lived through the war, the flag raised over Suribachi was the first news of victory to arrive in the midst of the hardest fighting—and the whole war's cost and will made visible.

title: 营长
source: 《营长》（Комбат），苏联摄影记者马克斯·阿尔佩特摄于1942年7月12日，伏罗希洛夫格勒（今卢甘斯克）近郊。画面要点：低机位仰视近景，一名军官立在高草坡上，右手高举TT手枪、大张着口呐喊下令冲锋，左臂向后挥出，胸前挂着望远镜与地图包；身后草丛中几名戴钢盔的士兵伏低持枪准备跃出，大块积云的天空占据画面大半。
story: 1942年7月12日，苏德战场南翼，德军夏季攻势正向伏罗希洛夫格勒（今卢甘斯克）压来。塔斯社摄影记者马克斯·阿尔佩特随一支部队准备反击：进攻发起前，一名军官从长草中站起身，右手举起TT手枪，向着队伍高喊冲锋。阿尔佩特迎着他按下了快门——只来得及拍这一张，几分钟后，这名军官中弹阵亡。阿尔佩特不知道他的名字，见他带队冲锋，便认定是营指挥员，照片由此得名《营长》。

照片当时并未发表，在阿尔佩特的个人收藏里躺了多年，直到1974年才在《真理报》刊出。读者的来信随之涌来，阿尔佩特花了两年时间调查，终于确认照片里的人：第220步兵团初级政治指导员阿列克谢·戈尔杰耶维奇·叶廖缅科，时年36岁——按制度他已免于征召，仍主动请战，阵亡前一天连长负伤，他代替连长带队。查找曾多年无果，因为同一营里还有一位姓名缩写相同的同姓学员，档案把两人混为一谈，他的家人收到的竟是『失踪』通知。叶廖缅科长眠在卢甘斯克州霍罗舍耶村附近的烈士合葬墓，村里的纪念碑复刻了照片中的姿态。
战后，《营长》成为卫国战争传播最广的照片之一：登上美国杂志封面，被印上苏联1985年胜利日的纪念邮票和1985年刚果的邮票，1995年俄罗斯『胜利50周年』纪念币也采用了它的剪影。照片记录的瞬间只有几秒——一名军官站起身、举枪、喊出进攻——却成了这场战争里个人勇气最被铭记的形象之一。

en.title: Battalion Commander
en.source: Kombat (Комбат, The Battalion Commander), taken by Soviet war photographer Max Alpert on July 12, 1942, near Voroshilovgrad (today Luhansk).
en.points: A low-angle close view: an officer stands on a slope of tall grass, right arm thrust high with a TT pistol, mouth wide open shouting the order to attack, left arm swept back, binoculars and a map case slung at his chest. Behind him helmeted soldiers crouch low in the grass with their rifles, ready to spring forward, and a sky of towering cumulus fills most of the frame.
story: On July 12, 1942, on the southern wing of the German-Soviet front, the German summer offensive was pressing down on Voroshilovgrad (today Luhansk). Max Alpert, a photographer of the TASS agency, was with a unit preparing a counterattack. Just before the attack went in, an officer rose out of the tall grass, lifted a TT pistol in his right hand, and shouted the charge to his men. Alpert pressed the shutter as the man bore toward him—there was time for that one frame only; minutes later the officer was shot and killed. Alpert never learned his name; seeing him lead the attack, he took him for a battalion commander, and the photograph has carried the title Kombat—Battalion Commander—ever since.

The picture went unpublished at the time and lay in Alpert's personal collection for years, appearing in Pravda only in 1974. Letters from readers came flooding in, and after two years of inquiry Alpert at last fixed the man in the frame: Alexei Gordeyevich Yeryomenko, junior political officer of the 220th Rifle Regiment, thirty-six years old—by rule exempt from conscription, he had asked to fight all the same; the day before his death, when the company commander was wounded, he led the company in his place. The search had long foundered because another cadet of the same battalion bore the same surname and initials, and the records confused the two; his own family had in fact been notified he was “missing.” Yeryomenko lies in the communal grave of the fallen near the village of Khorosheye in the Luhansk region, and the village memorial reproduces his pose from the photograph.

After the war Kombat became one of the most widely circulated photographs of the Great Patriotic War: it ran on the cover of an American magazine, was printed on a Soviet Victory Day commemorative stamp of 1985 and on a stamp of the Congo the same year, and its silhouette was used on Russia's “50th Anniversary of Victory” commemorative coin of 1995. The instant it records lasted but a few seconds—an officer rising, a pistol lifted, the attack called out—yet it became one of the most remembered images of personal courage in that war.

title: 邦克山号中弹
source: 美国海军官方照片，说明原文『USS Bunker Hill (CV-17) hit by two Kamikazes in 30 seconds on 11 May 1945 off Kyushu. Dead-372. Wounded-264.』，现藏美国国家档案馆。画面要点：从邻近舰艇拍摄的全景，中弹燃烧的航母腾起冲天烟柱，海面平阔、天色阴灰。
story: 1945年5月11日上午，冲绳战役期间，埃塞克斯级航空母舰邦克山号（CV-17）正随第五十八特混舰队在九州以南外海轮值警戒，舰队司令米切尔中将的指挥部就设在这艘船上。上午约10时，两架日军特攻机在30秒内接连撞上舰体：第一架零式战斗机由21岁的安野中尉驾驶，先扫射飞行甲板再俯冲撞入并投下炸弹，炸点周围停满加满油、挂好弹的待发舰载机；约半分钟后，22岁的小川清少尉驾驶彗星舰上爆击机穿过猛烈的防空炮火，撞进舰岛附近的甲板，引发更致命的大火。
官方战后清点：阵亡372人、负伤264人，算上后续伤重不治者，阵亡总数接近400人——这是美军单舰在单次特攻攻击中遭到的最高伤亡。全舰官兵与赶来支援的邻近舰艇整日奋战，至夜里将大火扑灭，保住了船体。邦克山号被拖回美国布雷默顿修理，但战争在它重返战场前就结束了：1947年除役，战后的现代化改装计划一拖再拖，最终再未服役，1973年售出拆解。
这张照片由美国海军摄影师在邻近舰艇上拍摄，现藏美国国家档案馆：冲天的浓烟柱与倾斜甲板上燃烧的机群，让它在战后成为神风特攻威胁与太平洋战争惨烈程度最有代表性的影像之一。

en.title: USS Bunker Hill Hit by Kamikazes
en.source: Official U.S. Navy photograph; original caption: “USS Bunker Hill (CV-17) hit by two Kamikazes in 30 seconds on 11 May 1945 off Kyushu. Dead-372. Wounded-264.” Held at the U.S. National Archives.
en.points: A panorama taken from a neighboring ship: the stricken, burning carrier sends a column of smoke towering into the sky; the sea lies flat and open under a gray overcast.
story: On the morning of May 11, 1945, during the Okinawa campaign, the Essex-class aircraft carrier USS Bunker Hill (CV-17) was flying her turn of alert duty with Task Force 58 in the waters south of Kyushu, the flagship of Vice Admiral Mitscher, the force commander, riding aboard. At about ten in the morning two Japanese special-attack aircraft struck the ship within thirty seconds. The first, a Zero fighter flown by 21-year-old Lieutenant Anno, strafed the flight deck, then dove in and crashed, releasing a bomb—parked thick around the point of impact were fueled and armed aircraft waiting to launch. About half a minute later, 22-year-old Ensign Kiyoshi Ogawa brought a D4Y Suisei (“Judy”) carrier dive bomber through the heavy anti-aircraft fire and crashed into the deck beside the island, touching off a still deadlier fire.

The official postwar reckoning: 372 dead and 264 wounded; counting those who later died of wounds, the dead came near to four hundred—the heaviest casualties inflicted on a single American ship in a single kamikaze attack. The crew, with the help of neighboring ships standing by, fought the fires through the day and had them out by night, saving the hull. Bunker Hill was towed home to Bremerton for repair, but the war ended before she could return to the line: decommissioned in 1947, her postwar modernization was put off again and again, she never served again, and in 1973 she was sold for breaking up.

The photograph, made by a U.S. Navy photographer aboard a neighboring ship, is held at the U.S. National Archives: the smoke towering into the sky and the aircraft burning across the tilting deck have made it one of the most representative images of the kamikaze menace and of the ferocity of the Pacific War.

title: 奥马哈滩头登陆
source: 《死亡之颚》（Into the Jaws of Death，原题 Taxis to Hell – and Back – Into the Jaws of Death），美国海岸警卫队摄影军士罗伯特·萨金特摄于1944年6月6日上午约7时40分，诺曼底奥马哈滩头『轻松红』（Easy Red）地段。画面要点：从登陆艇内部越过放下的艏跳板拍摄，一列美军士兵涉水冲向烟尘弥漫的滩头。
story: 1944年6月6日清晨7时40分，诺曼底登陆第一波突击开始：美国海岸警卫队队员操作的LCVP人员登陆艇把第1步兵师第16步兵团A连的士兵送上奥马哈滩头『轻松红』地段。艇艏跳板放下的一刻，海岸警卫队摄影军士罗伯特·萨金特就在艇内，拍下了这列士兵背着步枪装具、涉水冲向滩头的背影。照片最初的完整标题是《Taxis to Hell – and Back – Into the Jaws of Death》——开往地狱的出租车，一头扎进死亡之颚。
奥马哈是当天五个登陆滩头中战斗最惨烈的一个：德军第352步兵师依托高地与工事居高临下，首波部队被压制在水线附近数小时不得寸进，当天美军在奥马哈滩头伤亡约2400人。直到傍晚，盟军才在滩头真正立足。奥马哈的突破为盟军打开了通往内陆卡朗坦与圣洛方向的大门，诺曼底桥头堡由此连成一片。
这张照片后来成为整个D日最著名的影像之一，现藏美国国家档案馆。海岸警卫队在诺曼底负责操艇送步兵上滩与救捞落水者，萨金特按下的这一次快门，让艇上这些无名士兵的背影替整整一代人记住了那个上午。

en.title: Landing on Omaha Beach
en.source: Into the Jaws of Death (originally titled Taxis to Hell – and Back – Into the Jaws of Death), taken by Coast Guard Photographer's Mate Robert Sargent at about 7:40 on the morning of June 6, 1944, in the Easy Red sector of Omaha Beach, Normandy.
en.points: Shot from inside a landing craft past the lowered bow ramp: a line of American soldiers wades through the water toward the smoke-hung beach.
story: At 7:40 on the morning of June 6, 1944, the first assault wave of the Normandy landings went in: LCVP landing craft crewed by U.S. Coast Guardsmen carried soldiers of Company A, 16th Infantry Regiment, 1st Infantry Division, onto the Easy Red sector of Omaha Beach. At the moment the bow ramp fell, Coast Guard Photographer's Mate Robert Sargent, riding in the craft, caught the backs of that line of soldiers as they waded shoreward under rifle and gear. The photograph's first full title was Taxis to Hell – and Back – Into the Jaws of Death—the taxi down to hell, and the plunge into the jaws of death.

Omaha was the hardest fought of the five landing beaches that day: the German 352nd Infantry Division, from its high ground and works, looked down on the first waves and held them near the waterline for hours, and American casualties on Omaha that day came to about 2,400. Only by evening had the Allies a true footing ashore. The breakout at Omaha opened the way inland toward Carentan and Saint-Lô, and the Normandy beachhead was knitted whole.

The photograph became one of the most famous images of D-Day and is held at the U.S. National Archives. The Coast Guard's work at Normandy was to boat the infantry ashore and pull the drowning from the water; with this one press of the shutter Sargent let the backs of the nameless soldiers in his boat keep that morning in memory for a whole generation.

title: 国会大厦废墟
source: 《帝国国会大厦废墟》，1945年5月柏林战役结束后的档案照片，摄影师不详。画面要点：弹痕累累的国会大厦正立面与烧毁的穹顶钢架，门前广场布满瓦砾。
story: 1945年4月，柏林战役进入最后阶段。国会大厦自1933年国会纵火案后基本闲置，纳粹时期议会早已名存实亡，又历经多年空袭，到战役前已满目疮痍。它几乎没有军事价值，却仍是第三帝国无可替代的象征——朱可夫说，攻城部队需要的就是一个『显著的目标』。4月30日清晨，白俄罗斯第一方面军第3突击集团军第79步兵军下属的第150、第171步兵师对大厦发起强攻，守军包括党卫军、国防军残部、人民冲锋队与海军学员，逐层顽抗到5月2日才放下武器。
4月30日深夜，第150步兵师侦察兵米哈伊尔·叶戈罗夫与梅利通·坎塔里亚在中尉阿列克谢·别列斯特带领下，把胜利旗帜插上大厦山墙的雕塑，5月2日又将旗帜移上穹顶——这就是后来『胜利旗』的由来。大厦内部在战斗与火灾中烧成焦炭，墙面上则留满了苏军士兵用粉笔、刺刀和铅笔刻下的留言：谁的城市、谁的名字、为了谁。
战后大厦荒置多年，墙上的留言在历次整修中被刻意保留；两德统一后，建筑师诺曼·福斯特为它加上了新的玻璃穹顶，1999年起作为德国联邦议院所在地重新启用。这张战役刚结束时的废墟照片，记录的是帝国心脏的终结：一个政权在这里开始，也在这里化为瓦砾。

en.title: The Reichstag in Ruins
en.source: The Reichstag in Ruins, an archival photograph from after the close of the Battle of Berlin, May 1945; photographer unknown.
en.points: The shell-torn front of the Reichstag and the burnt steel skeleton of its dome; the square before the entrance is buried in rubble.
story: In April 1945 the Battle of Berlin entered its last stage. The Reichstag had stood largely unused since the arson of 1933—parliament under the Nazis had long been a thing of name only—and after years of air raids it was already scarred past recognition before the battle reached it. It held scarcely any military value, yet it remained the irreplaceable symbol of the Third Reich; Zhukov said the attacking troops needed exactly a “conspicuous target.” On the morning of April 30, the 150th and 171st Rifle Divisions of the 79th Rifle Corps, 3rd Shock Army, 1st Belorussian Front, stormed the building; its defenders—SS men, Wehrmacht remnants, Volkssturm, and naval cadets—held out floor by floor and laid down their arms only on May 2.

Late on April 30, Mikhail Yegorov and Meliton Kantaria, scouts of the 150th Rifle Division, led up by Lieutenant Alexei Berest, planted the Victory Banner among the statuary of the pediment, and on May 2 the flag was carried up to the dome—the origin of the later “Victory Banner.” The interior had burned to charcoal in the fighting and the fires, while the walls filled with what Soviet soldiers wrote and carved there in chalk, in bayonet point, in pencil: whose city, whose name, for whom.

The building stood vacant for years after the war, and the soldiers' inscriptions were deliberately kept through the successive restorations. After German reunification the architect Norman Foster crowned it with a new glass dome, and since 1999 it has served again as the seat of the German Bundestag. This photograph of the ruins, taken as the battle ended, records the finish of the heart of the Reich: a regime that began here came apart here, into rubble.

title: 国会大厦升旗
source: 《国会大厦上的胜利旗》（Знамя Победы над Рейхстагом），塔斯社摄影记者叶夫根尼·哈尔杰伊摄于1945年5月2日，柏林国会大厦楼顶。画面要点：低机位仰视，三名苏军士兵在檐口石雕间竖起红旗，远景是硝烟中的柏林。
story: 1945年5月2日，柏林城防刚放下武器，塔斯社随军摄影记者叶夫根尼·哈尔杰伊赶到了国会大厦。他从莫斯科出发时随身带着几面用红桌布缝成的旗——布料取自舅舅的布店。他后来说：『这一天我等了1400天』，从德军越过苏联边境算起，一天不多、一天不少。当天他带三名士兵登上大厦楼顶，请他们把旗插上檐口，按下了这张后来传遍全世界的照片：居中的士兵双手撑起旗杆探身向下，两名战友在石雕花饰间托扶着他。
在这之前，真正的升旗已经发生过：4月30日深夜，第150步兵师侦察兵叶戈罗夫与坎塔里亚把胜利旗插上大厦山墙，5月2日清晨移上穹顶；哈尔杰伊的照片是对那一幕的再现。照片发表前还被修版加工：画面中士兵手腕上多戴的手表被小心抹去——那是苏军劫掠行为的刺眼证据，背景也添上浓黑的硝烟，让场景看起来仍在激战。由于苏联媒体的保密惯例，画面中人物与摄影师本人的身份多年里一直存在争议。
争议之外，照片的力量没有减弱：它与硫磺岛折钵山升旗遥相对称，成为反法西斯胜利最通行的视觉符号之一，被数千种出版物转载。哈尔杰伊出身顿巴斯的犹太家庭，母亲死于1941年德军枪下；他此后拍过纽伦堡审判与1956年的布达佩斯，直到晚年才获得应有的承认，1997年在莫斯科去世。

en.title: Raising a Flag over the Reichstag
en.source: Banner of Victory over the Reichstag (Знамя Победы над Рейхстагом), taken by TASS war photographer Yevgeny Khaldei on May 2, 1945, on the roof of the Reichstag, Berlin.
en.points: From a low angle looking up: three Soviet soldiers set a red flag upright among the stone carving of the cornice, with smoking Berlin for a background.
story: On May 2, 1945, with the Berlin garrison just surrendered, Yevgeny Khaldei, TASS's front-line photographer, made haste to the Reichstag. He had left Moscow carrying several flags sewn from red tablecloth—the cloth came from an uncle's drapery shop. “I had waited 1,400 days for this day,” he said afterward—counted from the day the German armies crossed the Soviet border, to the day, not one more and not one less. That day he took three soldiers onto the roof, set them to planting the flag on the cornice, and pressed the shutter on the photograph that would soon run round the world: the soldier at center leans out over the drop with both hands on the pole, two comrades steadying him among the carved stone.

Before this, the true raising had already been: late on April 30, Yegorov and Kantaria, the scouts of the 150th Rifle Division, set the Victory Banner on the pediment, and on the morning of May 2 moved it to the dome; Khaldei's photograph was a restaging of that scene. Before publication it was retouched: the second wristwatch on a soldier's arm—glaring proof of looting by Soviet soldiers—was carefully painted out, and dense black smoke was laid into the background so that the scene should read as battle still burning. Under the secrecy habits of the Soviet press, the identities of the men in the frame, and for years even of the photographer himself, remained matters of dispute.

Dispute aside, the photograph lost none of its force: set beside the flagraising on Iwo Jima as its counterpart, it became one of the most current visual symbols of the victory over fascism, reprinted in thousands of publications. Khaldei came of a Jewish family in the Donbass; his mother was shot by the Germans in 1941. He photographed the Nuremberg trials, and Budapest in 1956, and came into his due recognition only late; he died in Moscow in 1997.

title: 东线步兵
source: 《东线的德军步兵》（German troops in Russia, 1941），美国国家档案馆缴获档案照，编号 NARA 540155，摄影师不详（应为德军宣传连随军摄影）。画面要点：堑壕豁口处，右侧德军步兵高举柄式手榴弹正要掷出，左侧一人持毛瑟步枪贴壕瞄准，身后是暗色森林。
story: 这张照片是美国国家档案馆收藏的缴获德军档案照，1941年摄于东线，摄影师不详，从取景与摆布的痕迹看，是国防军宣传连的随军作品：堑壕豁口处，一名步兵把柄式手榴弹高举过头正要掷出，身边的战友把毛瑟步枪架在壕沿上瞄准，身后是东欧无边无际的森林。它后来被反复翻印，成为德军步兵在东线作战最广为人知的形象之一。
1941年6月22日，德国入侵苏联，三百余万轴心国部队沿千里战线突入；经过明斯克、斯摩棱斯克与基辅的连续合围，德军中央集团军群于秋季兵临莫斯科城下。照片里的掷弹手与枪手正是这场攻势最前线的人物——每一枚掷出的手榴弹背后，都是步、坦、炮沿每一条村道与每一道堑壕的苦战。
东线从第一天起就是一场灭绝战争：纳粹把对苏战争定义为意识形态歼灭战，政委令、饥饿计划与对平民的报复屠杀随军而行。也正是在这条战线上，德军的攻势在1941年冬的莫斯科城下第一次折断，此后经斯大林格勒与库尔斯克，一步步走向1945年的覆灭。这张定格在攻势顶点的照片，回望时恰是那场浩劫起点处的剪影。

en.title: German Infantry on the Eastern Front
en.source: German troops in Russia, 1941, a captured German archival photograph held by the U.S. National Archives (NARA 540155); photographer unknown, in all likelihood a photographer of a Wehrmacht propaganda company.
en.points: At the open gap of a trench, the German infantryman at right holds a stick grenade lifted high, about to throw; at left a soldier aims a Mauser rifle along the trench lip; a dark forest stands behind them.
story: This photograph is one of the captured German army files held by the U.S. National Archives, made on the Eastern Front in 1941 by an unknown hand; the framing and the marks of posing identify it as the work of a Wehrmacht propaganda company. At the trench gap an infantryman holds a stick grenade over his head in the act of throwing; beside him his comrade lays a Mauser rifle across the trench edge and aims; behind them runs the dark, unending forest of eastern Europe. Reprinted and reprinted, it became one of the best-known images of the German infantryman's war in the East.

On June 22, 1941, Germany invaded the Soviet Union, and more than three million Axis troops drove in along a front of a thousand kilometers; after the great encirclements at Minsk, Smolensk, and Kiev, Army Group Center stood before Moscow in the autumn. The grenade-thrower and the rifleman of this photograph were men at the very spearpoint of that offensive—behind each grenade thrown lay the grinding of infantry, tanks, and guns along every village road and every trench line.

From its first day the Eastern Front was a war of extermination: the Nazi regime had defined the war on the Soviet Union as an ideological war of annihilation, and the Commissar Order, the Hunger Plan, and the reprisal killing of civilians marched with the armies. And it was on this front that the German offensive first broke, before Moscow in the winter of 1941, then worked its way down, through Stalingrad and Kursk, to the destruction of 1945. This frame, fixed at the crest of the offensive, looks in hindsight like a silhouette taken at the very head of the catastrophe.

title: 伞兵与滑翔机
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏（Bild 101I-569-1579-14A），署名 PK Fs AOK（伞兵军宣传连），摄于1943年9月的意大利，一次滑翔机着陆演练。画面要点：降落在草地上的DFS 230突击滑翔机旁，四名伞兵越过铁丝网离开机身投入行动。
story: 这张照片藏于德国联邦档案馆，由伞兵军宣传连的随军摄影拍摄，1943年9月摄于意大利，记录的是一次训练：一架DFS 230突击滑翔机降落在开阔草地上，四名伞兵正离开机身后投入行动——领头的一人抱着装具朝镜头跑来，脸上还带着笑意。
DFS 230是德国为突击空降专门研制的滑翔机，载一名飞行员与八至九名士兵，由Ju 52等飞机拖曳升空后无声滑翔落地。1940年5月，八十余名伞兵乘这种滑翔机直接降落在比利时埃本-埃马尔要塞顶上，一夜之间瘫痪了这座号称欧洲最坚固的要塞；1943年9月12日，又是DFS 230把突击队送上大萨索山顶，将被软禁的墨索里尼营救下山——与这张演练照正是同一个九月。
意大利退出战争后，德军伞兵部队在意大利半岛的山地节节设防，次年在卡西诺的废墟中死守数月，被盟军称作『绿色魔鬼』。这张轻松明快的演练瞬间，拍在那场漫长绞杀战开始之前。

en.title: Paratroopers with a DFS 230 Glider
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 101I-569-1579-14A, credited to PK Fs AOK (the paratroop army's propaganda company), taken in Italy in September 1943 at a glider landing exercise.
en.points: Beside a DFS 230 assault glider landed on the grass, four paratroopers leave the machine, crossing the wire as they go into action.
story: The photograph, in the German Federal Archives, was taken by the photographer of a paratroop propaganda company in Italy in September 1943, and records an exercise: a DFS 230 assault glider has landed on open grass, and four paratroopers are leaving the fuselage and going into action—the man in front runs toward the camera with his gear in his arms, a smile still on his face.

The DFS 230 was the glider Germany built expressly for assault landings: it carried one pilot and eight or nine soldiers, was towed into the air behind a Ju 52 or the like, and then cast off to glide down in silence. In May 1940, some eighty paratroopers in these gliders landed straight onto the roof of the Belgian fortress of Eben-Emael and put the reputedly strongest fortress in Europe out of action in a night; on September 12, 1943, it was again a DFS 230 that set the raiders on the Gran Sasso to bring Mussolini down from his mountain captivity—the same September as this exercise photograph.

After Italy quit the war, the German paratroop divisions laid their defensive lines through the mountain spine of the peninsula; the next year they held out for months among the ruins of Cassino, and the Allies named them the “Green Devils.” This light, bright moment on a training field was taken before that long war of attrition began.

title: 流泪的法国人
source: 《流泪的法国人》（The Weeping Frenchman），摄于1940年9月15日马赛，《生活》杂志1941年3月3日号『本周图片』刊出，摄影师不详。画面要点：人群中央一位穿细条纹西装的中年人泪水纵横，身旁众人神情凝重。
story: 这张被称为『流泪的法国人』的照片摄于1940年9月15日的马赛：法国陆军各团的团旗正被装船运往北非——按照停战后的安排，这些军团荣誉的最高象征必须离开本土，以免落入德国之手。人群中的一位中年人望着旗帜远去的方向热泪纵横。摄影师不详，《生活》杂志在1941年3月3日那一期把它刊为『本周图片』，原始说明是：『一个法国人为他的国家失陷团队的旗帜被放逐非洲而流下爱国悲痛之泪』。
半年多以前，法国刚经历了军事史上最彻底的崩溃之一：1940年5月德军穿越阿登，6月14日进入巴黎，6月22日签署停战协定，第三共和国终结，国土被切成德占区与维希政权治下的非占领区，军队解散。对亲历者来说，被运走的远不止几面绸旗，还有一支军队全部的过去与体面。
它的流传史本身就是一则关于档案的教训：美国国家档案馆曾把它误标为『1940年6月14日德军进入巴黎时，一个法国人在流泪』，这个错误的说明随着翻印流传了几十年，后来才被更正。而旗帜的故事还有结局：三年半之后的1944年8月，自由法国的第二装甲师开回巴黎，凯旋门上重新挂起三色旗——本组下一张照片定格的正是那个下午。

en.title: The Weeping Frenchman
en.source: The Weeping Frenchman, taken in Marseille on September 15, 1940; published as LIFE magazine's “Picture of the Week” in the issue of March 3, 1941; photographer unknown.
en.points: At the center of the crowd a middle-aged man in a pin-striped suit weeps openly, the faces around him grave.
story: The photograph known as “The Weeping Frenchman” was taken in Marseille on September 15, 1940: the regimental colors of the French Army were being shipped that day to North Africa—under the armistice terms, these supreme emblems of the regiments' honor had to leave metropolitan France lest they pass into German hands. A middle-aged man in the crowd watched toward the colors as they went, the tears running down his face. The photographer is unknown; LIFE printed the picture as “Picture of the Week” on March 3, 1941, under the original caption: “A Frenchman weeps tears of patriotic grief as the colors of his defeated country's regiments are sent into exile in Africa.”

A little more than half a year before, France had passed through one of the most complete collapses in the history of war: in May 1940 the German army came through the Ardennes; it entered Paris on June 14, and on June 22 the armistice was signed. The Third Republic was at an end, the country was cut into the German-occupied zone and the unoccupied zone under Vichy, and the army was dissolved. To those who lived it, what was being carried away was far more than a few silk flags: it was the whole past, and the whole honor, of an army.

The picture's own afterlife is a lesson in the care of archives: the U.S. National Archives long mistitled it “A Frenchman weeping on June 14, 1940, as German troops entered Paris,” and that wrong caption rode the reprints for decades before it was set right. And the story of the colors found its ending: three and a half years later, in August 1944, the Free French 2nd Armored Division fought its way back into Paris, and the tricolor hung again over the Arc de Triomphe—the very afternoon that the next photograph in this set fixes.

title: 凯旋门前的勒克莱尔
source: 《凯旋门前的勒克莱尔》，乔治·梅拉梅德摄于1944年8月26日，巴黎解放次日的星形广场凯旋门前。画面要点：勒克莱尔将军（右）与另一名法军军官立于门前，身后是《马赛曲》浮雕、垂挂的三色旗与第二装甲师的装甲车辆和官兵。
story: 1944年8月26日，巴黎解放的次日，大游行从星形广场的凯旋门下出发，香榭丽舍大街上人山人海。摄影师乔治·梅拉梅德在门下拍下这一帧：勒克莱尔将军（右）与另一名法军军官并肩而立，身后门墙上正是吕德的名作《马赛曲——1792年志愿军的出发》，三色旗从拱门间垂下，第二装甲师的装甲车辆停在广场上，官兵或坐或立。

勒克莱尔——本名菲利普·德·欧特克洛克，1902年生——1940年法国溃败中负伤被俘，逃出后辗转赴伦敦投奔戴高乐，为保护身在沦陷区的家人改用化名『勒克莱尔』。他在撒哈拉指挥自由法国部队，1941年克夫拉之战后立下著名的『克夫拉誓言』：不见法国的旗帜飘扬在斯特拉斯堡与梅斯上空，绝不放下武器。1944年8月1日，他麾下的第二装甲师在犹他滩登陆，两周后违令转向巴黎，8月24日夜率先突入市区——最先抵达市政厅的第9连『La Nueve』几乎全由西班牙共和派流亡者组成，战车都以西班牙内战的战场命名；8月25日，德军巴黎城防司令肖尔蒂茨签署投降书，把巴黎交给了勒克莱尔。
大游行之后，勒克莱尔率部在11月解放斯特拉斯堡，兑现了誓言；1945至46年他代表法国在远东接受日军投降，1947年在阿尔及利亚坠机身亡，1952年被追授法国元帅。这张照片里凯旋门上飘着的三色旗，正是马赛港那面被放逐的旗帜故事的结局。

en.title: Leclerc at the Arc de Triomphe
en.source: General Leclerc at the Arc de Triomphe, by Georges Mélamed, taken on August 26, 1944, the day after the liberation of Paris, before the Arc de Triomphe on the Place de l'Étoile.
en.points: General Leclerc (at right) and another French officer stand before the arch; behind them are the relief of La Marseillaise, tricolors hanging down, and the armored vehicles and soldiers of the 2nd Armored Division.
story: On August 26, 1944, the day after the liberation of Paris, the great march set out from beneath the Arc de Triomphe on the Place de l'Étoile, and the Champs-Élysées was packed from side to side. Under the arch the photographer Georges Mélamed took this frame: General Leclerc (at right) stands shoulder to shoulder with another French officer; on the pier behind them is Rude's masterpiece, La Marseillaise — the Departure of the Volunteers of 1792; tricolors hang down through the vault, and the armored vehicles of the 2nd Armored Division stand on the square with their soldiers sitting and standing about them.

Leclerc—born Philippe de Hautecloque in 1902—was wounded and taken prisoner in the French collapse of 1940. He escaped, made his way by roundabout routes to London and to de Gaulle, and took the assumed name “Leclerc” to shield the family he left in the occupied country. He commanded Free French troops in the Sahara, and after the fight at Kufra in 1941 swore his famous “oath of Kufra”: to lay down his arms only when the flag of France flew again over Strasbourg and Metz. On August 1, 1944, his 2nd Armored Division landed at Utah Beach; two weeks later, against its orders, it turned for Paris, and on the night of August 24 led the way into the city—the first unit to reach the Hôtel de Ville was the 9th Company, “La Nueve,” made up almost wholly of exiled Spanish Republicans, its carriers named for the battlefields of the Spanish Civil War. On August 25 the German commandant of Paris, von Choltitz, signed the capitulation and gave the city over to Leclerc.

After the march, Leclerc led the division to the liberation of Strasbourg in November and made his oath good; in 1945–46 he stood for France at the Japanese surrender in the Far East; he was killed in an air crash in Algeria in 1947, and in 1952 was posthumously raised to Marshal of France. The tricolor flying over the Arc de Triomphe in this photograph is the ending of the story of the colors exiled from Marseille.

title: 难民入租界
source: 《逃入上海公共租界的市民》（Citizens of Shanghai fleeing into Shanghai International Settlement - Battle of Shanghai (1937)），摄影师不详，1937年9月摄于上海。画面要点：街头难民潮全景，左侧钢桁架桥的桥腹与一辆车顶坐满人的老式卡车，人流扶老携幼漫过街面，有人推独轮车、有人用板车抬着病人，前景几名提包袱、扛行李的男子清晰可辨，众人皆着夏季短褂与长衫。
story: 1937年8月13日，淞沪会战在上海打响。战火最先烧到的闸北、虹口与杨树浦都是人口稠密的街区，数百万人从战区涌向宣布中立的租界——法租界与苏州河以南的半个公共租界。战前通行无阻的路口装上了铁栅门，外白渡桥成了从虹口进入公共租界的唯一通道，桥面上人流昼夜不息，租界最多时集中了七十多万难民。一位在场的美国人写道：难民们"像洪水一样汹涌而来——乘着卡车、客车、推车、独轮车、人力车，或者步行而来。扶老携幼，背负手提，婴儿坐在父辈的肩篮"。

这张照片拍摄于1937年9月的上海街头，正是难民潮最高峰的时候。照片背面印着日本出版战争史料《母と子でみる20世紀の戦争·日中戦争Ⅰ》的书页来源，画面里的人群与今天上海档案馆保存的同场景照片可以相互印证：同样的卡车、同样的桥头、同样望不到头的人流。挤进租界并不意味着安顿——露宿街头的难民成年人每日冻饿死者以百计，儿童更多。11月，法国神父饶家驹在方浜路以北划出南市难民区，至1940年关闭时保护了约三十万平民，这一实践后来被写进了1949年《日内瓦第四公约》的中立区条款。

en.title: Refugees into the Concessions
en.source: Citizens of Shanghai fleeing into Shanghai International Settlement - Battle of Shanghai (1937), photographer unknown, taken in Shanghai in September 1937.
en.points: A street panorama of the refugee flood: at left the belly of a steel truss bridge and an old truck with people packed on its roof; the current of humanity, old and young together, crosses the street—some push wheelbarrows, some carry the sick on flatcarts; in the foreground several men with bundles and shoulder-loads stand out clearly; all about are summer jackets and gowns.
story: On August 13, 1937, the Battle of Shanghai broke out. The quarters the fighting struck first—Zhabei, Hongkou, Yangshupu—were the most thickly peopled in the city, and millions pressed out of the battle zone toward the concessions that had declared neutrality: the French Concession, and the half of the International Settlement south of Suzhou Creek. Iron-barred gates closed the crossings that before the war had stood open to all; the Garden Bridge became the one passage left from Hongkou into the International Settlement, its deck streaming with people day and night; at the height of it the concessions held more than 700,000 refugees. One American on the spot wrote that they came “like a flood—by truck, by bus, by handcart, by wheelbarrow, by rickshaw, or on foot; the old with the young on their arms, backs loaded and hands full, babies riding in the shoulder-baskets of their fathers.”

This photograph was taken on a Shanghai street in September 1937, at the very crest of the flood. The back of the print bears its source: a page of the Japanese wartime pictorial 母と子でみる20世紀の戦争·日中戦争Ⅰ (The 20th Century Seen with Mother and Child: The Sino-Japanese War I); the crowd in the frame can be set against photographs of the same scene kept today in the Shanghai Archives—the same truck, the same bridgehead, the same unending stream of people. Getting inside the concession did not mean getting safe: of the refugees sleeping in the open streets, adults died of cold and hunger by the hundred each day, and children in greater number still. In November the French priest Father Jacquinot drew the boundary of the Nanshi Refugee Zone north of Fangbang Road; by its closing in 1940 it had sheltered some 300,000 civilians, and the practice was written in after years into the neutral-zone provisions of the Fourth Geneva Convention of 1949.

title: 淞沪迫击炮阵地
source: 《淞沪会战中以迫击炮攻击日军的国民革命军》（National Revolutionary Army attacking the Japanese army by motar artillery in the Battle of Shanghai (1937)），摄影师不详，约1937年8月摄于淞沪战场。画面要点：近景，伪装枝叶覆盖的迫击炮组阵地上，左侧一名士兵双手高举迫击炮弹正要装填，中间一名士兵立姿观察前方，右侧一名士兵俯身在炮尾操作，全身插满树叶伪装。
story: 1937年8月13日开始的淞沪会战，是中国军队在抗战初期投入最大的一场会战：七十余个师、约七十万人先后投入上海及周边的水网地带，对阵逐步增兵至二十余万的日军。在缺乏重炮与空中掩护的条件下，轻便的迫击炮是中国步兵手中最重要的支援火力——金陵兵工厂仿制的八十二毫米迫击炮构造简单、拆开即可人力搬运，能在水网田埂间跟随步兵转移，在罗店、大场一线的拉锯战中一再压制日军的机枪阵地。

这张照片摄于1937年8月前后的淞沪前线，摄影师不详。画面里的迫击炮组给自己插满了枝叶伪装——在没有制空权的战场上，白天任何暴露的火器都会招来日军飞机与舰炮的报复。三个人各司其职：一人送弹，一人观察，一人操炮，动作压到最低。淞沪会战打了整整三个月，中国军队伤亡约二十五万人，11月12日上海陷落；但正是这三个月打破了日军"三个月灭亡中国"的打算，沿海的工厂、学校与博物馆得以西迁，为持久战保住了家底。

en.title: Mortar Position, Battle of Shanghai
en.source: National Revolutionary Army attacking the Japanese army by motar artillery in the Battle of Shanghai (1937) (title as originally catalogued), photographer unknown, taken on the Shanghai battlefield around August 1937.
en.points: A close view of a mortar position under leafy camouflage: at left a soldier lifts a mortar shell high in both hands to load it; at center a soldier stands watching to the front; at right a soldier bends over the barrel of the piece, his whole body stuck about with leaves.
story: The Battle of Shanghai, begun on August 13, 1937, was the largest single engagement Chinese forces fought in the opening period of the War of Resistance: more than seventy divisions, on the order of 700,000 men, were fed into the creek-woven country about Shanghai, against a Japanese force that mounted by degrees past 200,000. Without heavy guns and without cover from the air, the light mortar was the greatest supporting fire in the Chinese infantryman's hands: the 82mm mortar built at the Jinling Arsenal to a foreign pattern was simple in the making, broke down into man-loads, followed the infantry along the field paths between the paddy dikes, and beat down Japanese machine-gun nests again and again in the see-saw fighting before Luodian and Dachang.

The photograph was taken on the Shanghai front about August 1937; the photographer is unknown. The crew in the frame have stuck themselves full of leafing boughs—on a field without command of the air, any weapon that showed itself by daylight drew the answer of Japanese aircraft and naval shells. Three men, three parts: one passes the shell, one watches, one serves the tube, every motion pressed to its least. The battle for Shanghai ran its full three months and cost the Chinese forces some 250,000 casualties before the city fell on November 12; but those three months broke the Japanese reckoning of “finishing China in three months,” and the factories, schools, and museums of the coast went west, keeping the means of a long war.

title: 台儿庄巷战
source: 《台儿庄战役》（Battle of Taierzhuang），摄影师不详，1938年4月摄于台儿庄城内。画面要点：低机位随队拍摄，几名背背包、持步枪的中国士兵沿两侧断壁残垣的街道奔跑冲锋，砖墙倒塌、木梁裸露，远处街道深处更多士兵的身影跟进，地面铺满瓦砾。
story: 1938年3月下旬，日军第十师团濑谷支队沿津浦线北段南犯，进抵鲁南小镇台儿庄。防守此处的是第五战区司令长官李宗仁麾下孙连仲第2集团军，城内主力为池峰城第31师。3月27日，日军在重炮掩护下炸塌北城墙突入城内，双方随即在不足两平方公里的街巷中逐屋争夺：日军占了北街，守军就翻上屋顶投手榴弹；街巷被夺，敢死队夜里再摸回来。守军把手榴弹和大刀用到了极致——整个战役期间第31师消耗手榴弹约三十万枚，数百名敢死队员身绑手榴弹、臂缠白毛巾，一夜之间夺回城西北角四分之三的阵地，五十七人的队伍最后只剩十三人。
4月6日晚，李宗仁下令全线反攻，城外汤恩伯第20军团自侧背合围，城内守军倾力出击。4月7日清晨，台儿庄城内日军被歼殆尽，残部向北溃退。此役中国军队以三万将士伤亡的代价歼灭日军一万余人，是全面抗战以来正面战场取得的第一次重大胜利，武汉数十万人连夜提灯游行庆祝。这张巷战照片就摄于城内争夺最激烈的那些天：奔跑的士兵身后，是已经被炮火犁过一遍的台儿庄。

en.title: Street Fighting in Taierzhuang
en.source: Battle of Taierzhuang, photographer unknown, taken within the town of Taierzhuang in April 1938.
en.points: Shot low, moving with the party: Chinese soldiers with packs and rifles run the charge down a street lined with broken walls, brickwork fallen in and roof beams bare; deeper down the street the shapes of more soldiers follow; the ground is paved with rubble.
story: In the last days of March 1938 a detached brigade group of the Japanese 10th Division came south along the northern reach of the Tianjin–Pukou railway and reached Taierzhuang, a small town in southern Shandong. Holding it under Li Zongren, commander of the Fifth War Zone, was Sun Lianzhong's 2nd Army Group, the chief strength in the town being Chi Fengcheng's 31st Division. On March 27 the Japanese breached the north wall under a storm of heavy shell and broke into the town, and for days after, the two sides fought for it house by house within barely two square kilometers: when the Japanese took the north streets, the defenders went up on the roofs to throw grenades down; when a lane was lost, the dare-to-die parties stole it back by night. Grenades and the great two-handed sword were worked to the uttermost—through the whole battle the 31st Division spent some 300,000 grenades, and parties of dare-to-die men, grenades bound to their bodies and white towels about their arms, took back three-quarters of the ground at the town's northwest corner in a single night; of one party of fifty-seven men, thirteen were left.

On the night of April 6 Li Zongren ordered the counterattack along the whole line: Tang Enbo's 20th Army Group closed in on the Japanese flank and rear outside the town while the defenders within threw their last strength out. By the morning of April 7 the Japanese in Taierzhuang were destroyed wellnigh to a man, and the broken remnant fled north. The battle cost the Chinese some 30,000 casualties against upward of 10,000 Japanese killed—the first great victory won on the regular front since the all-out war began; in Wuhan hundreds of thousands walked the night with lanterns in celebration. This photograph of street fighting was taken in the sharpest days of the struggle for the town: behind the running soldiers lies Taierzhuang, already ploughed over once by the guns.

title: 史102出击前
source: 中华民国海军官方照片《"史102"快艇出击前的伪装》（Disguising Shi 102 Boat Before the Strike, Aug 1937），1937年8月摄于长江内河沿岸。画面要点：岸滩边一艘鱼雷快艇侧靠水面，艇身罩着半圆拱状的伪装棚架，数名艇员在甲板上作业，艇艏与艇艉的低矮轮廓贴着平静的江面。
story: 淞沪会战爆发时，黄浦江里泊着日本海军第三舰队的旗舰"出云"号——日军侵华海军的指挥中枢。中国海军与日军实力悬殊，主力舰队自沉于江阴封锁线后，能动的水面兵力里最锋利的一把刀，是电雷学校所属的英制鱼雷快艇。1937年8月14日晚，快艇大队副大队长安其邦率"史102"号（艇长胡敬端）与"史171"号伪装成民船，昼隐夜行沿内河潜驶上海；"史171"途中故障，"史102"于15日晚独自抵达龙华。16日白天，两名军官化装成商人侦察了"出云"号泊位，当晚八时，"史102"号高速冲过黄浦江上的日舰与各国军舰，在距"出云"号约三百米处连射两枚鱼雷。

鱼雷炸毁了"出云"号周围的防雷网与码头驳船，未能击沉目标，返航的"史102"号被日舰炮火击中油箱，搁浅在九江路税关栈桥附近，官兵拆下艇上武器泅水登岸，月余后才辗转返回江阴。这张照片拍的是出击之前：为了瞒过沿途与江面上的耳目，整艘快艇被罩进半圆拱状的伪装棚架，伪装成一条内河民船。日方战后评述，这次袭击"是中国海军唯一的一次积极攻击手段"——一艘小小的快艇，替一支几乎打光了的海军留下了主动进攻的记录。

en.title: Shi 102 Before the Strike
en.source: Official Navy of the Republic of China photograph, “Disguising Shi 102 Boat Before the Strike, Aug 1937,” taken in August 1937 along an inland waterway of the Yangtze.
en.points: At the water's edge a torpedo boat lies alongside, its hull housed in a half-round arched camouflage frame; several of the crew work on deck, the low lines of bow and stern resting on the calm river.
story: When the Battle of Shanghai opened, the flagship of the Japanese Navy's Third Fleet, the Izumo, lay in the Huangpu—the command heart of Japan's naval war in China. The Chinese Navy stood far below its enemy in strength; after the main fleet was scuttled by its own hands to close the Jiangyin blockade, the sharpest blade among the surface forces still able to move was the British-built torpedo boat of the Dianlei School. On the night of August 14, 1937, An Qibang, deputy commander of the torpedo boat group, took Shi 102 (boat captain Hu Jingduan) and Shi 171 toward Shanghai dressed up as merchant craft, hiding by day and running the creeks by night; Shi 171 broke down on the way, and Shi 102 reached Longhua alone on the evening of the 15th. In the daylight of the 16th two officers, dressed as traders, scouted out the Izumo's berth; at eight that evening Shi 102 tore at full speed down the Huangpu past the Japanese warships and the ships of every flag, and from some three hundred meters off the Izumo fired her two torpedoes.

The torpedoes tore up the anti-torpedo netting and the pier lighters about the Izumo but did not sink her; on the way back Shi 102 was struck in her fuel tank by Japanese gunfire and went aground near the customs pier off Jiujiang Road. Her crew took off what weapons the boat carried, swam ashore, and after more than a month worked their way back to Jiangyin. The photograph was made before the strike: to blind the eyes along the banks and on the river, the whole boat was housed in a half-round arched frame, made up as an inland cargo boat. Japanese postwar comment called the attack “the Chinese Navy's one act of positive offence”—one small boat keeping for a nearly spent navy the record of going over to the attack.

title: 人拉石磙
source: 美国陆军官方照片《数百名中国民工拉石磙平整机场跑道》（Hundreds of Chinese laborers pull a roller to smooth a runway for an airstrip），美国陆军摄于1944年3月，中国西南的B-29前进机场工地。画面要点：广角全景，上百名民工排成横贯画面的长队，腰间纤索共同拖曳一台巨型石磙碾压跑道，大块积云的天空占据画面上半，碎石铺就的跑道延伸向远处的树丛与小丘。
story: 1943年底，中美商定"马特霍恩"计划：以中国西部的机场群为基地，用B-29远程轰炸机直接轰炸日本本土。国民政府随即启动代号"特种工程"的机场修建，要求在半年内于成都平原新建扩建新津、邛崃、彭山、广汉四个轰炸机机场。1944年1月，四川二十九个县紧急征调的五十余万民工自带锄头、扁担与口粮开进工地，其中不少是妇女和孩子。跑道要承受六十吨重的轰炸机起降，路基厚达一米，所需的鹅卵石把岷江、沱江两岸的河滩捞空，全部靠肩挑背扛运到工地。

没有压路机，民工们就用混凝土浇筑的巨型石磙代替——最重的十几吨，需要上百人一起拉。石磙轴心穿铁柱、系上几十米长的主绳，两侧再分出细绳，每个民工把绳套勒在肩上，指挥员举旗吹哨，号子声里千百人同时发力，拖着石磙一层一层把跑道碾实。5月，四个机场如期交付；6月16日夜，六十八架B-29从成都平原起飞，首炸日本九州八幡的钢铁基地。美国空军博物馆至今陈列着一尊从中国运去的石磙，旁边悬挂着几百名中国民工拉磙碾轧跑道的巨幅照片，说明牌上写着：Runways By Hand——用双手铺造的跑道。

en.title: Pulling the Stone Roller
en.source: Official U.S. Army photograph, “Hundreds of Chinese laborers pull a roller to smooth a runway for an airstrip,” taken by the U.S. Army in March 1944 at a forward B-29 airfield construction site in southwest China.
en.points: A wide-angle panorama: upward of a hundred laborers in a line reaching across the frame haul together, by tow-ropes at their waists, a giant stone roller over the runway; a sky of towering cumulus fills the upper half, and the gravel runway runs out toward distant trees and low hills.
story: At the close of 1943 China and the United States settled the Matterhorn plan: to fly B-29 long-range bombers against the Japanese home islands from the airfield cluster of western China. The National Government at once opened the airfield works under the code name “Special Project”: four bomber fields at Xinjin, Qionglai, Pengshan, and Guanghan on the Chengdu Plain, new-built or expanded, all within half a year. In January 1944 more than half a million laborers, hastily conscripted from twenty-nine counties of Sichuan, marched onto the works carrying their own hoes, shoulder-poles, and rations; among them were many women and children. The runways must bear bombers of sixty tons; the subgrade ran a meter thick, and the cobblestones it asked for stripped the river beaches of the Min and the Tuo bare, every stone carried to the works on backs and shoulders.

There were no road rollers, and the laborers set giant rollers cast in concrete in their place—the heaviest ran to a dozen tons and more, and asked a hundred men and more to pull. An iron axle passed through the roller's heart, a head-rope of tens of meters was made fast to it, and from the head-rope the side-ropes branched; each man set the rope over his shoulder, the ganger lifted his flag and blew his whistle, and to the chant a thousand backs heaved at once, and the roller went over the runway course by course. In May the four fields were delivered on their day; on the night of June 16, sixty-eight B-29s lifted from the Chengdu Plain and struck for the first time the iron and steel works at Yawata on Kyushu. The National Museum of the U.S. Air Force keeps to this day one of the stone rollers brought over from China, hung beside a great photograph of hundreds of Chinese laborers hauling a roller across a runway, with a card beside it that reads: Runways By Hand.

title: 难民火车
source: 《桂林大疏散》（Evacuation of Kweilin, September 1944），美国陆军照片，1944年9月摄于桂林火车站。画面要点：月台全景，一列客车停在人群中，车顶坐满难民、行李在车顶堆成小山，车窗里外全是攀爬的人影，月台上人山人海，前景几名穿制服戴白帽者的背影把视线引向车厢。
story: 1944年，日军发动规模空前的豫湘桂会战，旨在打通大陆交通线。6月长沙陷落，8月衡阳苦守四十七天后失守，日军沿湘桂铁路直逼广西。9月8日，桂林城防司令部发出第二号疏散令；9月12日的第三号命令要求全城居民在14日正午前离城，逾期以汉奸论处。此时这座城里还挤着四十多万人——既有桂林市民，也有从湖南一路逃难来的难民。火车成了唯一的指望：北站南站人山人海，列车没有时刻表，每一节车厢都塞得满满当当，车顶坐人、机车两侧扒人、车厢底下的轮架上都搭着木板躺人。

作家秦牧夫妇是徒步走出广西的；6岁的琼瑶随家人挤上了这样的火车，她后来在回忆录里把难民火车的位置分成三等："上位"高踞车顶，日晒夜露；"中位"在车厢里，人贴人站着都能睡着；"下位"最险——车轮之间的铁条上架木板躺着，鼻尖顶着车底，身侧是旋转的车轮。9月14日正午过后，桂林全城疏散完毕，城中"只见军人，不见平民"。11月，桂林陷落。这张美国陆军照片定格的正是9月那几天桂林车站的样子：一列列车像负重的昆虫爬离战火，把一座空城留给即将到来的炮声。

en.title: The Refugee Train
en.source: Evacuation of Kweilin, September 1944, a U.S. Army photograph taken at Guilin (Kweilin) railway station in September 1944.
en.points: A full view of the platform: a passenger train stands within a sea of people, its roof covered with refugees and the luggage heaped on it into little hills; figures climb in and out of the windows on both sides; the platform is packed solid, and in the foreground the backs of several men in uniform and white caps lead the eye toward the carriages.
story: In 1944 the Japanese army opened its Henan–Hunan–Guangxi campaign (Operation Ichi-Go), of a scale without precedent, to drive its corridor through the mainland railways. Changsha fell in June; Hengyang was lost in August after forty-seven days of defense; and the Japanese pressed down the Hunan–Guangxi line into Guangxi. On September 8 the Guilin city defense headquarters issued its second evacuation order; the third, on September 12, required every soul in the city to be out by noon on the 14th, on pain of being held a traitor. The city still held more than four hundred thousand people—the citizens of Guilin and the refugees come all the long way from Hunan. The trains were the one hope: north station and south station were seas of people, no train kept a timetable, every car was packed past filling—men rode the roofs, clung on either side of the engine, and lay on planks laid across the wheel-frames beneath the cars.

The writer Qin Mu and his wife walked out of Guangxi; six-year-old Chiung Yao and her family squeezed aboard just such a train, and in her memoirs she sorted the places on a refugee train into three ranks: the “upper seat” rode high on the car roof, in the sun by day and the dew by night; the “middle seat” stood within the car, where men slept upright pressed one against another; the “lower seat” was the most perilous of all—boards laid across the iron between the wheels, the nose against the floor of the car, the spinning wheels alongside. After noon on September 14 the city stood wholly emptied, “soldiers only, and no civilians to be seen.” In November Guilin fell. This U.S. Army photograph fixes the Guilin station in those September days: train after train crawling from the fire like an insect under load, leaving an empty city to the guns on their way.

title: 学生兵
source: 《中国学生队开赴前线》（Chinese Student's Corps members starting for the front, Battle of Changsha, 1941-1942），美国海军国家博物馆藏战时照片（藏品号 Lot 11614-7），摄于1941年12月至1942年1月第三次长沙会战期间。画面要点：中近景，一名年轻的学生兵侧脸清晰，头戴缀青天白日帽徽的军帽，背包带交叉勒在胸前，肩上斜背步枪，身旁战友背着圆顶斗笠，背景土坡后有列队的队伍。
story: 1941年12月24日，日军第十一军再犯长沙，中国第九战区司令长官薛岳以"天炉战法"且战且退，把日军诱入长沙外围的合围圈，1942年1月4日发起总攻，1月15日战役结束，重创日军——这是太平洋战争爆发后盟军阵营对日军的第一次重大陆上胜利，各国驻华使节与新闻界云集长沙战后现场，美国海军也把这组照片收进自己的战时宣传照片档案。原始说明写道："中国青年是战斗的一代。战争爆发以来，中国已训练了二十余万青年男女奔赴各条战线，肩并肩地战斗。"
照片里的这支学生队伍就是在这样的动员潮中走上前线的：学生利用课余受训，编队开赴前线担任宣传、救护、运输与通信等战地工作，队伍里不乏未成年的少年。画面中央的少年兵侧脸朝前，军帽的帽徽、交叉的背包带与肩上的步枪都已配齐，嘴唇微张，像正跟着队伍喊着口号。当这个国家的正规军在一寸山河一寸血地苦战时，课堂里最年轻的一代已经把行军背包背上了肩。

en.title: Student Soldiers
en.source: Chinese Student's Corps members starting for the front, Battle of Changsha, 1941–1942, a wartime photograph held by the National Museum of the U.S. Navy (Lot 11614-7), taken during the Third Battle of Changsha, December 1941 into January 1942.
en.points: A medium-close view: the profile of a young student soldier in sharp focus, his cap bearing the white-sun-on-blue-sky emblem, the pack straps crossed tight over his chest, a rifle slung across his shoulder; beside him a comrade carries the round conical field hat, and behind the earthen slope a formed body of men stands in line.
story: On December 24, 1941, the Japanese 11th Army came at Changsha once again. Xue Yue, commander of the Ninth War Zone, worked his “heavenly furnace” way of war—fighting and giving ground to draw the Japanese into the ring of encirclement about the city's approaches; the general attack opened on January 4, 1942, the battle closed on January 15, and the Japanese were badly hurt. It was the first great land victory won over the Japanese army on the Allied side since the Pacific War broke out; the envoys and the press of many nations gathered at Changsha after the fight, and the U.S. Navy took this set of photographs into its own wartime archive. The original caption read: “China's youth is a fighting generation. Since the war began, China has trained more than 200,000 young men and women, who have gone to the fronts to fight shoulder to shoulder.”

The student unit in the photograph went up to the front on just such a tide of mobilization: students trained outside school hours and marched off in formed units to field work—propaganda, rescue, transport, signals—and boys under age were no rarity in the ranks. The young soldier at the frame's center turns his profile forward; cap badge, crossed pack straps, and the rifle on his shoulder are all in place, the lips a little parted, as if calling the pace to a slogan. While the country's regular armies fought their war of blood for every inch of ground, the youngest generation of the schoolrooms had already shouldered its marching packs.

title: 骡队拖炮
source: 美国陆军通讯兵照片（编号 SC 196168），格林伯格技术军士（T/Sgt Greenberg）摄于1944年9月9日，云南滇西，一支十骡骡队拖曳重炮沿山路开赴董岭（Tung Ling）一带的战斗途中，现藏美国国家档案馆。画面要点：高机位俯瞰，山道弯弯，十匹骡子排成纵列拖曳覆着伪装网的炮车与前车，数名炮兵骑骡随行，一名戴斗笠的驭手走在头骡前牵引，山林葱郁、山峦层叠。
story: 1944年5月11日，中国远征军Y部队强渡怒江，发起滇西反攻：第二十集团军仰攻高黎贡山，围攻腾冲；第十一集团军沿滇缅路苦战龙陵，又在松山与日军死守的堡垒群逐坑争夺。滇西全是高山深谷，公路被翻毁，重武器全靠骡马运上前线——炮兵把山炮与榴弹炮拆成几大件驮在骡背上，或像这张照片里那样用十几匹骡子整炮拖曳，在之字形山道上一天爬不了几十里。美军为此派出了骡马运输与兽医分队协同作战。

9月上旬，战斗正到最紧处：9月7日松山光复，9月14日腾冲城内巷战结束，全城夷为焦土，龙陵还在反复拉锯。9月9日，通讯兵格林伯格在滇西的山道上按下了这张快门：十匹骡子的炮队正翻过山路弯道，驭手的斗笠、骡背上的汗光与层层远山，是这场反攻最日常也最吃力的一幕。1945年1月，滇西反攻与驻印军缅北反攻在芒友会师，中印公路全线打通，第一批车队于2月4日抵达昆明——滇西的每一门拖过山的炮，都是这条路的前身。

en.title: Mule Team Hauling the Howitzer
en.source: U.S. Army Signal Corps photograph (SC 196168), by T/Sgt Greenberg, taken on September 9, 1944, in western Yunnan: a ten-mule team hauling a howitzer along a mountain road on its way toward the fighting at Tung Ling; held at the U.S. National Archives.
en.points: From a height looking down: the mountain road winds, ten mules in single file hauling the net-camouflaged gun carriage and its limber, several gunners riding mules alongside, a driver in a broad field hat leading the foremost mule by the head; the forest deep green, the ranges folded one behind another.
story: On May 11, 1944, the Chinese Expeditionary Force's Y Force forced the crossing of the Salween and opened the counteroffensive in western Yunnan: the 20th Group Army climbed the Gaoligong range against Tengchong and closed the town in; the 11th Group Army fought its way up the Burma Road at Longling, and at Songshan wrestled pit by pit with the fortress the Japanese had made of the hill. Western Yunnan is all high mountains and deep valleys, the roads torn up, and the heavy weapons came forward on mule and horse: the artillery broke its mountain guns and howitzers into loads for the mules' backs, or, as in this photograph, hauled the gun entire behind a string of a dozen animals, and a day's climb on the switchbacks might not make tens of li. The Americans sent pack-transport and veterinary detachments to work alongside.

In the first ten days of September the fight stood at its tightest: Songshan was retaken on September 7; the street fighting in Tengchong ended on September 14, the whole city burnt to waste; Longling still see-sawed. On September 9 the Signal Corps photographer Greenberg pressed the shutter on a mountain road of the west: the ten-mule gun train swinging round the bend of the road, the driver's field hat, the sweat on the mules' backs, and the ranges folding behind—the most everyday and the most punishing turn of the counteroffensive. In January 1945 the Yunnan counteroffensive joined hands at Mangyou with the counteroffensive in northern Burma of the Chinese forces in India, the China–India road was opened through from end to end, and the first convoy rolled into Kunming on February 4—every gun dragged over the mountains of western Yunnan was the making of that road.

title: 紧急起飞
source: 皇家空军官方摄影师 H. 亨瑟摄于1939年11月，法国里尔近郊的塞克兰机场（Lille-Seclin），帝国战争博物馆藏（C 468）。画面要点：低机位平视略仰，87中队的飞行员们沿对角线从左前向右后奔向草地上排列的飓风战斗机，最前者大幅摆臂冲刺，有人提着飞行帽、有人背着降落伞包，晴日长影。
story: 1939年9月战争爆发，英国远征军渡海开进法国，皇家空军的一支随行兵力进驻法国北部机场，其中装备飓风战斗机的87中队（绰号『联合省』中队）进驻里尔近郊的塞克兰机场，为远征军担任空中掩护。此后几个月西线几乎没有战事，史称『假战争』：飞行员们每天的工作是巡逻、警戒，与一遍又一遍演练紧急起飞。
这张照片摄于1939年11月的一次演练：警报响起，飞行员们从待命室冲出，跑向停在草地上的飓风。随军的皇家空军官方摄影师亨瑟按下了快门，画面里他们跑成一列斜线——最前的人全力冲刺，有人一手拎着飞行帽，有人背着降落伞包。帝国战争博物馆的说明还记下一个细节：此时运抵法国的部分替换飓风已换上三叶变距螺旋桨，而较早到货的仍是双叶木桨，两种桨在同一场演练里并存。
平静只维持到来年5月：德军攻势一起，驻法空军在消耗战中且战且退，87中队于6月撤回英国，随即投入不列颠空战，编入第10大队保卫西南英格兰，队中出了伊恩·格里德与罗兰·比蒙特这样的名字。这张『假战争』时期演练照里的从容与速度，与几个月后的血战恍如两个世界。

en.title: Scramble
en.source: By the official Royal Air Force photographer H. Hensser, taken in November 1939 at Lille-Seclin airfield near Lille, France; Imperial War Museum (C 468).
en.points: Shot low, level, a little upward: the pilots of No. 87 Squadron run on the diagonal from front left toward the Hurricanes ranged on the grass, the man in the lead sprinting with great swings of the arms, one with his flying helmet in hand, one with a parachute pack on his back—long shadows on a clear day.
story: When war broke out in September 1939 the British Expeditionary Force crossed to France, and a part of the Royal Air Force went with it onto the airfields of the north; among them No. 87 Squadron, flying Hurricanes, took its post at Lille-Seclin near Lille to stand air cover over the army. For months after, the Western Front was nearly still—the “Phoney War”: the pilots' working day was patrols and readiness, and the scramble practiced over and over.

The photograph was taken at one such practice in November 1939: the alarm went, the pilots ran from the readiness room toward the Hurricanes standing on the grass, and Hensser, the RAF's official photographer with them, caught them strung out on the slant—the man in front at his full sprint, one with the flying helmet in his fist, one with the parachute pack on his back. The Imperial War Museum caption keeps one detail more: some of the replacement Hurricanes now out to France had been given three-blade variable-pitch airscrews, while the earlier machines still wore the two-blade wooden one, and both stood together at the same practice.

The quiet held only to May of the next year: when the German offensive broke, the air force in France fell back fighting a losing match of attrition; No. 87 Squadron came home in June, went straight into the Battle of Britain under No. 10 Group in defense of the southwest of England, and gave the service such names as Ian Gleed and Roland Beamont. The composure and the speed of this Phoney War practice look, set against the bloodletting a few months on, like the picture of another world.

title: 敦刻尔克海滩
source: 摄于1940年5月末敦刻尔克撤退期间，敦刻尔克近郊的布雷迪讷沙滩，摄影师不详，出自皇家阿尔斯特步枪队军官 H. E. N. 布雷丁的战时收藏，现藏帝国战争博物馆（HU 1137）。画面要点：高机位俯瞰，成百的第2营士兵背对镜头坐在沙滩斜坡上面向大海等待撤离，左侧一列纵队沿沙滩行进，远处海面空阔、烟霭沉沉。
story: 1940年5月，英国远征军随盟军在比利时崩溃，被压向敦刻尔克的滨海地带。5月26日『发电机行动』开始，皇家海军与征用的民船昼夜往返，到6月4日把约33.8万名军人撤回英国——他们中的大多数是从海滩涉水登上小艇、再转运到大船上去的。

皇家阿尔斯特步枪队第2营这一次留在外围后卫线上。6月1日凌晨2时30分，该营奉命放弃阵地向海滩转移，沿沙滩东行，在布雷迪讷一处以沉入水中的卡车和跳板搭成的临时码头等候接驳；船迟迟不来，全营又继续步行到敦刻尔克港的防波堤，上午11时许登上驱逐舰回国，一路德机不断扫射轰炸海岸。全营伤亡与被俘约170余人。这张照片出自该营军官布雷丁的战时收藏：成百的步枪兵坐在沙滩上，背对镜头面向大海，队列依然整齐——等待，是敦刻尔克海滩上最常见的姿态。
战后，皇家阿尔斯特步枪队因该营在敦刻尔克外围的坚守与断后获得『敦刻尔克1940』战斗荣誉。这张照片入藏帝国战争博物馆，成为记录敦刻尔克海滩最著名的影像之一。

en.title: The Beach at Dunkirk
en.source: Taken during the Dunkirk evacuation at the end of May 1940, on the sands of Bray-Dunes near Dunkirk; photographer unknown; from the wartime collection of Royal Ulster Rifles officer H. E. N. Bredin; Imperial War Museum (HU 1137).
en.points: From a height looking down: hundreds of soldiers of the 2nd Battalion sit with their backs to the camera on the shelving sand, facing the sea as they wait for evacuation; at the left a single file marches along the beach; far out the water lies open and the haze hangs heavy.
story: In May 1940 the British Expeditionary Force, falling with its allies from the collapse in Belgium, was pressed into the coastal strip about Dunkirk. Operation Dynamo opened on May 26; the Royal Navy and the small craft taken up from trade ran the passage day and night, and by June 4 had brought home about 338,000 men—the greater part of them wading from the beaches into the little boats, to be lifted out to the greater ships.

The 2nd Battalion, Royal Ulster Rifles, stood this time upon the outer guard line. At half past two on the morning of June 1 it was ordered off its ground and down to the beaches; marching east along the sand, it waited at Bray-Dunes by a landing place improvised from lorries sunk in the water and duckboards; when the boats were long in coming, the whole battalion walked on to the moles of Dunkirk harbor, and about eleven in the morning went aboard destroyers for home, under German aircraft strafing and bombing the coast the whole way. Its killed, wounded, and taken came to about 170 men. The photograph comes from the wartime collection of the battalion's officer Bredin: hundreds of riflemen sitting on the sand, backs to the camera, faces to the sea, their order still unbroken—waiting was the commonest posture of the beaches of Dunkirk.

After the war the Royal Ulster Rifles received the battle honour “Dunkirk 1940” for the 2nd Battalion's holding and covering on the outer perimeter. The photograph passed into the Imperial War Museum, and stands among the best-known images of the beaches of Dunkirk.

title: 地铁站之夜
source: 英国新闻部摄影处摄影师（佚名）摄于1940年，伦敦奥德维奇地铁站（Aldwych），帝国战争博物馆藏（D 1675）。画面要点：沿站台纵深拍摄，避难的伦敦人成两列坐卧——站台边一列、停用的轨道上一列——盖着大衣睡在毯子里，墙面高处挂着一排大衣，站台灯光沿纵深渐暗。
story: 1940年9月7日，德军对伦敦的持续空袭开始，史称大轰炸。官方起初并不打算把地铁用作防空洞，但每天黄昏，成千上万伦敦人自带毯子枕头涌向车站，拒不离开；既成事实之下，地铁站在当年秋天正式开放为夜间避难所，一些停运路段拆去线路、垫平轨道，也睡满了人。
奥德维奇站平日客流稀少，战时干脆停运，整座车站改作防空洞：没有床，人们每晚自带被褥下到站台睡下，清晨再把一切随身带走。新闻部摄影师1940年拍下这一幕：沿站台望去，人们成两列睡去——一列在站台边上，一列就在停用的轨道里；墙面高处挂着一排大衣，那是第二天清晨要穿的外衣。
大轰炸持续到1941年5月，伦敦人在地铁里度过了无数这样的夜晚。奥德维奇站在战后恢复有限运营，1994年永久关闭；如今它是伦敦交通博物馆『隐秘伦敦』参观线路上的保留一站，站台还是照片里的样子。

en.title: Night in the Underground
en.source: By an unnamed photographer of the Ministry of Information Photographic Division, taken in 1940 at Aldwych underground station, London; Imperial War Museum (D 1675).
en.points: Shot down the length of the platform: sheltering Londoners lie and sit in two lines—one along the platform edge, one in the disused track—sleeping under coats and in blankets; a row of overcoats hangs high along the wall, and the platform lamps go down into darkness with the distance.
story: On September 7, 1940, the German air offensive against London began in earnest—the Blitz. At first the authorities had no thought of turning the Underground to shelter; but every evening thousands of Londoners came down to the stations with blankets and pillows under their arms, and would not go; faced with the fact, the tube was opened that autumn as a formal night shelter, and on some closed stretches the track was lifted and the bed leveled flat—and these, too, filled with sleepers.

Aldwych, never a busy station, was closed outright in wartime and given over wholly to shelter: there were no bunks; people brought their own bedding down to the platform each night and carried every stick of it away at dawn. A Ministry of Information photographer took the scene in 1940: down the platform, the sleepers in two files—one at the platform edge, one in the disused tunnel itself—and high along the wall a row of overcoats: the coats they would put on again in the morning.

The Blitz ran on into May 1941, and Londoners passed unnumbered such nights in the tube. Aldwych went back to limited service after the war, and closed for good in 1994; today it is a stop kept on the London Transport Museum's “Hidden London” tours, the platform still much as it stands in the photograph.

title: 废墟中的读书人
source: 福克斯图片社摄影师哈里森摄于1940年10月23日，伦敦肯辛顿荷兰宫图书馆废墟，照片经战时新闻检查机关以皇家版权首发。画面要点：平视室内，三名穿西装大衣戴礼帽的男子沿烧焦的高大书架墙一字排开——一人伸手取书、一人捧读、一人侧立观望，屋顶焚毁塌落，天光从豁口斜射而入。
story: 荷兰宫始建于1605年，本是伊丽莎白时代的豪宅，18到19世纪成为伦敦辉格党名流聚会的沙龙，长期属于福克斯家族。1940年9月27日夜，二十二枚燃烧弹在一场十小时的空袭中落在这座建筑上，大火几乎烧毁整座府邸，只有东翼和图书馆的大部分藏书奇迹般留存下来。
不到一个月后的10月23日，福克斯图片社摄影师哈里森走进图书馆废墟，拍下了这张照片：三名穿西装大衣、戴礼帽的男子就着从坍塌屋顶斜射下来的天光，在烧焦的书架墙前翻检书籍。照片经战时新闻检查机关以皇家版权首发，随即传遍世界，成为『伦敦打不垮』的象征。后世研究者指出，这一幕很可能是应召摆拍的宣传场景——但书是真书，废墟是真废墟。
战后宅邸荒置，1952年家族把遗址卖给伦敦郡议会，残垣成了荷兰公园的一部分，露天剧场与绿地就在昔日的花园里，图书馆的断墙至今立在园中。这张照片的原件藏于历史英格兰档案馆，是大轰炸时期流传最广的伦敦影像之一。

en.title: Readers among the Ruins
en.source: By Fox Photos photographer Harrison, taken on October 23, 1940, in the ruins of the Holland House library, Kensington, London; first published under Crown copyright through the wartime press censorship.
en.points: An interior at eye level: three men in suits and coats and hats stand ranged along the wall of tall scorched bookcases—one reaching for a book, one reading one in his hands, one standing by looking on; the burned roof has fallen in, and the daylight slants in through the breach.
story: Holland House, first raised in 1605, was a great Elizabethan seat that became, through the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, the salon of London's Whig grandees, long in the keeping of the Fox family. On the night of September 27, 1940, twenty-two incendiary bombs fell upon it within one raid of ten hours; the fire all but ate the mansion, and only the east wing and the greater part of the library's books came through, as if by miracle.

Barely a month after, on October 23, Harrison, a photographer of the Fox Photos agency, walked into the ruins of the library and made this photograph: three men in suits and coats and hats, in the daylight slanting through the broken roof, searching the books along the wall of scorched shelving. Passed by the wartime censor and first published under Crown copyright, it ran round the world at once, an emblem of “London can take it.” Later students have pointed out that the scene was very likely staged for the cameras—but the books were true books, and the ruin a true ruin.

The house lay waste after the war; in 1952 the family sold the site to the London County Council, the broken walls went into the making of Holland Park—the open-air theatre and the green standing now in the old gardens—and the shattered walls of the library rise in the park to this day. The vintage print of this photograph is held at the Historic England Archive; it stands among the most widely circulated London images of the Blitz.

title: 救火之夜
source: 摄影师不详，摄于约1941年伦敦一次周六夜空袭之后，纽约时报巴黎局收藏，现藏美国国家档案馆（编号541902）。画面要点：低机位平视，五名消防员在前景合力持水枪向右上方燃烧的临街建筑射水，水柱成弧线，一二层窗口火舌翻卷、浓烟蔽空，街道湿滑反光。
story: 大轰炸期间的伦敦消防员面对的是夜复一夜的火海：燃烧弹与高爆弹把整片街区点成火炬，他们通宵压水，天亮时瘫在路边。战前伦敦的消防力量并不雄厚，正规队之外靠1938年组建的辅助消防队扩充人手；空袭最烈的时候，消防员常在落弹未停时就得上前。
1941年8月，全国消防总队成立，把全国约一千六百支地方消防队收编为一支统一的国家队伍，成为英国消防史上的分水岭。这张摄于约1941年的照片记录的是一次周六夜空袭之后：五名消防员合力压住一支水枪，向一栋临街燃烧的建筑射水——水柱的弧线、翻卷的火舌与湿亮的街面，正是大轰炸最后阶段一个再寻常不过的夜晚。
这张照片的原件藏于美国国家档案馆的纽约时报巴黎局收藏——那是报社巴黎分社在战争年月里收集的欧洲战况影像，战后整批入档。几十年来它被反复翻印，成为表现伦敦大轰炸的标志性照片之一。

en.title: Firemen of the London Blitz
en.source: Photographer unknown, taken after a Saturday-night air raid on London, about 1941; from the New York Times Paris Bureau collection, now held at the U.S. National Archives (541902).
en.points: Level, from low down: five firemen in the foreground hold a hose branch together, playing the water onto the burning street-front building at the upper right; the jet arcs, flame rolls from the first- and second-floor windows, the smoke shuts out the sky, and the wet street shines with reflections.
story: The London fireman of the Blitz faced a sea of fire night upon night: incendiary and heavy bombs lit whole streets of the city into torches; the crews held water on them through the dark, and dropped where they stood when day came. London's firefighting strength before the war was not great, and beyond the regular brigades the Auxiliary Fire Service, raised in 1938, filled the ranks out; at the worst of the raids the firemen often had to go in while the bombs were still falling.

In August 1941 the National Fire Service was formed, and drew the country's sixteen hundred-odd local brigades into a single national body—the dividing line of British firefighting history. This photograph, taken about 1941, records the aftermath of one Saturday-night raid: five firemen together holding down a branch, driving the water onto a burning street-front building—the arc of the jet, the flame rolling at the windows, the wet shining street: the plainest ordinary night of the last stage of the Blitz.

The original print lies in the New York Times Paris Bureau collection at the U.S. National Archives—the European war imagery the paper's Paris office gathered through the war years, and deposited whole after it. Reprinted decade upon decade, it has become one of the signature photographs of the London Blitz.

title: 废墟上的茶水车
source: 英国新闻部摄影处摄影师（佚名）摄于1941年，伦敦一处刚清理完的轰炸废墟，帝国战争博物馆藏（D 2169）。画面要点：平视，右侧妇女志愿服务队的流动餐车开着窗口柜台，车后断墙残立；清废墟的先锋队工人坐在前排木板堆上手捧搪瓷杯喝茶吃点心，后方有人在窗口排队。
story: 1938年，眼见战争难以避免，内政部请雷丁侯爵夫人斯特拉·艾萨克斯出面组建妇女志愿服务队（WVS），协助防空民防事务。开战时它已有十六万余名成员，到1941年底突破百万，几乎渗入战时生活的每个角落，被誉为『世界上最伟大的女性队伍』。
空袭开始后，WVS的流动餐车成为废墟上最可靠的一景：为消防员、救援队与清墟工人送茶送饭，一车一壶，风雨无阻。这张1941年的照片里，清墟的是陆军先锋队的工人——他们刚把一处被炸民宅清理完毕，房主能取走的遗物已经取走，剩下的只有木料与碎砖；工人们坐在清出来的木板上，人手一杯茶，就着点心歇这一刻钟。
帝国战争博物馆保存着这辆餐车同一个上午的整组底片：排队、递茶、卸下成箱的点心，一帧一帧都是废墟上的日常。战后WVS延续服务至今，即今天的皇家志愿服务社。

en.title: Tea Van in the Ruins
en.source: By an unnamed photographer of the Ministry of Information Photographic Division, taken in 1941 at a freshly cleared bomb site in London; Imperial War Museum (D 2169).
en.points: At eye level: at the right the Women's Voluntary Services mobile canteen stands with its serving hatch open, a broken wall still standing behind it; the Pioneer Corps workmen who cleared the site sit in front on stacks of planks, enamel mugs of tea and buns in their hands, and behind them a queue waits at the hatch.
story: In 1938, with war plain in view, the Home Office asked Stella, Marchioness of Reading, to found the Women's Voluntary Services (WVS) to carry the load of civil defense against air attack. At the outbreak it counted more than 160,000 members; by the end of 1941 it had passed the million, and its hands were in almost every corner of wartime life; it was called “the greatest women's service in the world.”

When the raids began, the WVS's mobile canteens became the surest sight upon the rubble: tea and food carried out to the firemen, the rescue parties, and the clear-up gangs—van upon van, kettle upon kettle, in all weathers. In this photograph of 1941 the men at the site are Pioneer Corps workmen: they have just finished clearing a bombed dwelling-house; what the owners could take away has been taken, and there is nothing left but timber and broken brick; the men sit on the planks they have cleared, a mug of tea in every hand, taking their quarter of an hour with a bun.

The Imperial War Museum keeps the whole run of negatives from that same morning: the queue, the tea passed up, the crates of buns swung down—frame after frame of the plain day's work upon the rubble. The WVS served on past the war and serves still, as today's Royal Voluntary Service.

title: 搜救犬里普
source: 英国新闻部摄影处摄影师（佚名）摄于1941年8月，伦敦东区波普拉的空袭废墟，帝国战争博物馆藏（D 5945）。画面要点：平视略俯，一名戴钢盔穿民防大衣的防空哨员在瓦砾坡上弓身半蹲、回手向身后招呼同事，他前方的杂种梗犬立在砖堆顶低头嗅探，背景是断墙与木梁。
story: 1940年，防空哨员金在波普拉一处重灾现场捡到一只饿坏的杂种梗犬，收留了它，取名里普，南希尔街B132哨所的同事们把它当成了吉祥物。不久大家发现，这只没受过任何训练的狗天生会找人：在砖堆里嗅嗅扒扒，就能定出废墟下被困者的位置。
一年之间，里普参与寻获的空袭遇难者与幸存者数以百计，成为防空部门第一只名副其实的搜救犬；它的成功，促使官方此后认真组建搜救犬队伍。这张照片摄于1941年8月的波普拉：里普在砖堆顶上嗅定了位置，哨员回头看一眼，抬手向身后的同事们招呼——帝国战争博物馆的说明里写道，这位哨员很可能就是当年收养它的金本人。
1945年7月，里普获颁授予服役动物的迪金勋章，嘉奖词是『在1940年大轰炸中寻获众多空袭遇难者』。1946年里普去世，安葬在伦敦伊尔福德的PDSA动物公墓，是那里安葬的第一位迪金勋章得主；2009年，它的勋章在伦敦拍出两万四千余英镑。

en.title: Rip the Rescue Dog
en.source: By an unnamed photographer of the Ministry of Information Photographic Division, taken in August 1941 amid the air-raid rubble of Poplar, East London; Imperial War Museum (D 5945).
en.points: Level, a little downward: an air-raid warden in steel helmet and civil-defense coat crouches half-bent on the rubble slope, reaching back to wave up his colleagues; ahead of him the mongrel terrier stands atop the heap of bricks, head down and scenting; broken wall and roof timbers behind.
story: In 1940 an air-raid warden named King picked up a starving mongrel terrier at a heavily hit place in Poplar, took him in, and called him Rip; the men of post B132 in Southill Street made him their mascot. Before long they found that the dog, never trained a day in his life, could find people by nature: a turn of sniffing and scrabbling among the bricks, and he would fix the place of a victim lying trapped beneath the rubble.

Within the year, Rip had a hand in finding air-raid victims, dead and living, by the hundred, and stood as the first true search-and-rescue dog of the air-raid services; his success set the authorities, in the years after, to building search-dog teams in earnest. This photograph was taken in Poplar in August 1941: Rip has taken his scent and stands atop the bricks, and the warden, one look back, lifts his hand to call up the men behind—the Imperial War Museum caption notes that this warden is very likely King himself, the man who took Rip in.

In July 1945 Rip was awarded the Dickin Medal, the decoration for animals in service, cited for “finding many casualties of the air raids in the Blitz of 1940.” He died in 1946, and was laid to rest at the PDSA animal cemetery in Ilford, London—the first recipient of the Dickin Medal buried there; in 2009 his medal was sold at auction in London for more than twenty-four thousand pounds.

title: 豪号的炮组
source: 皇家海军官方摄影师 R. G. G. 库特中尉摄于1942年8月豪号战列舰服役前后，帝国战争博物馆藏（A 11760）。画面要点：平视略仰，八联装维克斯2磅『砰砰』炮的炮管成束指向天空，炮位周围水兵各就其位——操炮、传递长条弹夹、抱弹箱待命，背景是舰体结构与海面。
story: 豪号是英王乔治五世级战列舰的五号舰，也是最后服役的一艘：船厂资源优先给了商船与护航舰艇，它拖到1942年8月29日才升旗入列。服役当月，皇家海军官方摄影师库特中尉随舰拍下成组照片——试航、全速航行、舰员列队与这座砰砰炮位，同属帝国战争博物馆的一整个序列。
『砰砰』炮是维克斯2磅马克八世炮的绰号，皇家海军的标准近距防空炮：八根炮管束成一座，以长条弹夹供弹，射速如连珠，是军舰对抗俯冲轰炸机与低空攻击机的最后一道火力网。敦刻尔克之后，皇家海军把防空当作生死科目，豪号服役时装六座八联装砰砰炮，此后仍不断加装。
豪号先随本土舰队为北极船队护航，1943年参加西西里岛登陆的掩护，1944年调往东方舰队，再编入英国太平洋舰队，1945年在冲绳战役中炮击日军机场，熬过了整场战争，1958年解体。这幅服役之初的炮组照片里，水兵们各就各位传递弹夹——那是它漫长战程开始前的样子。

en.title: The Pom-Pom Crew of HMS Howe
en.source: Official Royal Navy photograph by Lt R. G. G. Coote, taken around the commissioning of the battleship HMS Howe in August 1942; Imperial War Museum collection (A 11760).
en.points: At eye level, tilted slightly upward: the eight barrels of a Vickers 2-pounder pom-pom mounting point skyward in a bundle; around the gun the sailors stand at their stations — laying the gun, passing the long strip ammunition clips, standing by with ammunition boxes — with the ship's structure and the sea behind.
story: Howe was the fifth ship of the King George V class of battleships and the last to commission: with shipyard capacity going first to merchant ships and escort vessels, she did not hoist her colours until 29 August 1942. In the month she commissioned, the Royal Navy's official photographer Lt Coote took a set of photographs aboard — sea trials, full-speed runs, crew musters and this pom-pom gun position — all one sequence held by the Imperial War Museum.

The pom-pom was the nickname of the Vickers 2-pounder Mark VIII, the Royal Navy's standard close-range anti-aircraft gun: eight barrels clustered into a single mounting, fed from long strip clips, firing so fast it sounded like its own name — the last curtain of fire a warship could throw against dive bombers and low-flying attackers. After Dunkirk the Royal Navy treated anti-aircraft defence as a matter of life and death: Howe commissioned with six eight-barrelled pom-pom mounts and kept adding more throughout the war.

Howe served first with the Home Fleet, escorting the Arctic convoys; in 1943 she covered the landings in Sicily; in 1944 she transferred to the Eastern Fleet and then to the British Pacific Fleet, and in 1945 bombarded Japanese airfields during the Okinawa campaign. She came through the whole war and was broken up in 1958. This photograph of the gun crew at the start of her service — sailors at their stations, passing clips — shows her as she was before the long years of her war began.

title: 逃难路上
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏（Bild 146-1971-083-01），署名特里奇勒（Tritschler），摄于1940年6月19日，法国卢瓦尔河畔日安（Gien）附近。画面要点：逃难路上，一名穿浅色罩裙的妇人牵着满载家当的辎重马车走在前头，左侧老爷车顶捆着行李，车后跟着狗。
story: 1940年5月10日，德军在西线发起进攻，荷兰、比利时相继陷落，6月初战火烧进法国北部。政府下令疏散，数以百万计的法国与比利时平民带着随身细软涌上向南的公路：有人开汽车，有人赶马车，更多的人推着自行车、拉着婴儿车，在轰炸与流言里往卢瓦尔河方向走。6月14日德军进入巴黎，6月17日贝当广播求和，可路上的难民并没有停下来——停战要到6月22日才签署，而公路上的车队已经走了整整一个月。这张照片由德国联邦档案馆藏，署名特里奇勒，原始说明写着：『难民的大车高高地装着他们仅存的少许家当。法国，日安附近，1940年6月19日。』

日安是卢瓦尔河畔的古城，正当南逃路线的咽喉。6月15日中午，德军炸弹第一次落在城里，城堡院内一发就炸死19人，横跨卢瓦尔河的大桥随后被炸断；6月19日前后，比利时与法国的难民队伍仍源源不断地从这座燃烧的城市边经过，同时存在的另一张档案照片记录的正是『1940年6月19日，日安逃难路上的比利时人与法国人』。照片里的妇人牵着马走在自己的家当前头，木轮大车的木架上挂着铁皮桶，一辆二十年代末式样的老爷车跟在旁边，车顶捆着铺盖——整个国家在路上。
法国人后来把这段经历称作『逃难』（l'Exode）。据战后统计，约有六百万到八百万人在这年春夏离开家园，占当时法国人口的五分之一。他们中的大多数在停战后的夏天陆续回乡，却发现家已划在德占区或非占领区的另一侧。这张由随德军行动的摄影者拍下的照片，留存了那场大迁徙中最普通的一幕：走，牵着马，带着能带走的一切。

en.title: On the Refugee Road
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 146-1971-083-01; credited to Tritschler, taken on 19 June 1940 near Gien on the Loire, France.
en.points: On the road of flight, a woman in a light-coloured smock walks ahead leading a wagon loaded high with household goods; to the left an old car with luggage roped to its roof, and a dog following behind.
story: On 10 May 1940 the German army attacked in the west; the Netherlands and Belgium fell in turn, and in early June the fighting burned its way into northern France. The government ordered evacuation, and millions of French and Belgian civilians took the roads south with whatever they could carry: some in cars, some with horse-drawn wagons, more pushing bicycles or pulling prams, walking toward the Loire through bombing and rumour. German troops entered Paris on 14 June, and Pétain broadcast his request for an armistice on 17 June, but the refugees on the roads did not stop — the armistice would not be signed until 22 June, and the columns had already been a full month on the move. The photograph, held by the German Federal Archives and credited to Tritschler, carries the original caption: refugee wagons loaded high with the little their owners have left. Near Gien, France, 19 June 1940.

Gien, an old town on the Loire, sat squarely at the throat of the southern escape routes. At midday on 15 June German bombs fell on the town for the first time; a single one killed nineteen people in the courtyard of the castle, and soon afterwards the bridge across the Loire was broken. Around 19 June, columns of Belgian and French refugees were still streaming past the burning town — another archival photograph from the same day records Belgians and French on the road of flight near Gien, 19 June 1940. The woman in the picture leads her horse ahead of her household goods; tin pails hang from the wooden frame of the high-sided farm cart, and a car of late-1920s vintage travels alongside with bedding roped to its roof — a whole nation on the road.

The French later gave the experience its own name: l'Exode, the Exodus. Postwar estimates put the number who left their homes that spring and summer at six to eight million, about a fifth of France's population. Most made their way home over the summer that followed the armistice, only to find that home now lay on the far side of the line between the occupied and unoccupied zones. This photograph, taken by a photographer travelling with the German army, preserves the most ordinary scene of that great migration: walking on, leading the horse, carrying everything that could be carried.

title: 蒂兰的战俘
source: 德国战地摄影记者埃里希·博夏特（Eric Borchert，1911–1941）摄于1940年5月23日上午，比利时埃诺省蒂兰（Thulin）村。画面要点：碎石路上，法军第158步兵团的战俘纵队迎面走来，居中的高个士兵直视镜头，右侧一名围围巾的伤兵双手捂住胸口，薄雾中的白杨与砖房退向远处。
story: 1940年5月23日，法兰西战役第十四天。比利时中部的蒂兰村一带，法军第43步兵师第158步兵团被德军第269步兵师下辖的第469步兵团击溃，成建制的抵抗就此瓦解：上午，幸存的官兵脱下钢盔，沿着村中的碎石路走向德军设在村口的收容线。随第469团行动的德国战地摄影记者埃里希·博夏特拍下了这支纵队——走在前面的士兵把行军毯卷成双股斜挎在肩上，一名颈部围着手帕、外披大衣的伤兵双手按住胸口一步一步往前挪，队伍里也有来自殖民地的士兵。他们身后，是薄雾里稀疏的白杨与砖房。

对法军来说，1940年五六月间的溃败以战俘营为终点：约一百五十余万法国军人在六周内被俘，其中约七千五百名殖民地士兵死在押运与监禁途中，黑人战俘还常遭就地处决。蒂兰的这支纵队只是最早的一批。博夏特1911年生于爱森纳赫，1941年10月10日死于托布鲁克前线，年仅三十岁；他在法国战役期间拍摄的底片于1945年被法军在斯特拉斯堡缴获，今藏法国国防部军史档案局。这张照片的原始说明准确到部队番号——『1940年5月23日于比利时蒂兰被第469步兵团俘获的法军第158步兵团（第43步兵师）战俘』——是那场崩溃留下的少数清晰的近景之一。

en.title: Prisoners at Thulin
en.source: German war photographer Erich Borchert (1911–1941), taken on the morning of 23 May 1940 in the village of Thulin, province of Hainaut, Belgium.
en.points: On a road of crushed stone, a column of prisoners of the French 158th Infantry Regiment marches toward the camera; the tall soldier in the centre looks straight into the lens, at the right a wounded man with a scarf holds both hands to his chest, and poplars and brick houses recede into thin mist.
story: 23 May 1940, the fourteenth day of the Battle of France. Around the village of Thulin in central Belgium, the French 158th Infantry Regiment of the 43rd Infantry Division was broken by the German 469th Infantry Regiment, part of the 269th Infantry Division, and organised resistance came apart: in the morning the survivors took off their helmets and walked down the village's stone road toward the German collection line at its edge. Erich Borchert, a German war photographer attached to the 469th Regiment, photographed the column — the soldier at the front carries his blanket rolled double across his shoulder; a wounded man, a handkerchief at his neck and a coat over it, presses both hands to his chest as he moves forward step by step; men from the colonies march in the ranks too. Behind them stand the sparse poplars and brick houses of the mist.

For the French army, the defeat of May and June 1940 ended in prisoner-of-war camps: about one and a half million French soldiers were captured within six weeks; some 7,500 colonial troops among them died in transit or in captivity, and Black prisoners were frequently shot out of hand. The column at Thulin was only among the first. Borchert, born in Eisenach in 1911, was killed at the Tobruk front on 10 October 1941, thirty years old; the negatives from his French campaign were seized by the French at Strasbourg in 1945 and are held today in the historical archives of the French Ministry of Defence. The original caption of this photograph is exact down to the unit numbers — prisoners of the French 158th Infantry Regiment (43rd Infantry Division) taken by the 469th Infantry Regiment at Thulin, Belgium, on 23 May 1940 — one of the few sharp, close records left by that collapse.

title: 比尔哈凯姆突击
source: 英国帝国战争博物馆藏（E 13313），伦纳德·切特温（Leonard Chetwyn，第1陆军电影与照相分队）摄于1942年6月12日，利比亚比尔哈凯姆。画面要点：低机位，沙漠开阔地上，自由法国外籍军团士兵跃出沙丘向敌支撑点冲刺，白船帽与卡其热带作训服在正午阳光下泛白，天空占去画面大半。
story: 1942年5月26日，隆美尔的非洲装甲军团发起加扎拉战役，防线南翼支点就是比尔哈凯姆——利比亚沙漠里一座干涸的古井要塞。守卫它的是科尼格准将指挥的自由法国第1旅，约三千七百人，核心是第十三外籍军团半旅：这里面有逃避纳粹的德国犹太人，有西班牙内战的老兵，还有日后的法国总理皮埃尔·梅西耶。从5月27日起，意德军队轮番强攻，飞机与重炮把棱形阵地犁了一遍又一遍，要塞整整守了十六天，牵制住隆美尔的半数兵力。6月10日至11日夜，科尼格奉命率部突围，约两千七百人踩着自己雷区的通路冲了出去。

这张照片由英军第1陆军电影与照相分队的伦纳德·切特温拍摄，帝国战争博物馆的原始说明标注于1942年6月12日：『自由法国外籍军团士兵"从沙漠中跃起，冲击一个敌军支撑点"』——战役尾声阶段的图景。画面里的军团士兵头戴标志性的白色船形帽，卡其衬衫与短裤，绑腿一直裹到膝下，起身的一瞬全队压成一条向前的斜线。次日，中东英军总司令奥金莱克发出通电：『联合国应当对比尔哈凯姆的法国部队及其英勇的将军科尼格满怀钦佩与感激。』
