比尔哈凯姆之后，『法国仍在战斗』不再只是一句广播词。戴高乐说，这座沙漠要塞向世界证明：贝当签署停战的那支军队之外，还有一支没有投降的法国军队。伦敦、开罗与伦敦广播里，比尔哈凯姆成了自由法国的第一个大战役名字；战后，巴黎塞纳河上一座桥改名『比尔哈凯姆桥』，桥头铜牌刻着：『在比尔哈凯姆，1942年5月27日至6月11日，自由法国第一旅击退了两个敌师疯狂冲击，向世界表明法国从未停止战斗。』

en.title: The Charge at Bir Hakeim
en.source: Imperial War Museum collection (E 13313); Leonard Chetwyn, No. 1 Army Film and Photo Section, taken on 12 June 1942 at Bir Hakeim, Libya.
en.points: From a low camera position on open desert ground, Free French Foreign Legion men spring over a dune and sprint toward an enemy strongpoint; white sailor caps and khaki tropical drill bleach out under the noon sun, and the sky fills most of the frame.
story: On 26 May 1942 Rommel's Panzer Army Africa opened the Battle of Gazala, and the anchor of the line's southern end was Bir Hakeim — an old fortified well-place in the Libyan desert. Holding it was the 1st Free French Brigade under Brigadier Koenig, some 3,700 men, its core the 13th Demi-Brigade of the Foreign Legion: among them German Jews fleeing Nazism, veterans of the Spanish Civil War, and a future prime minister of France, Pierre Messmer. From 27 May the Italian and German armies attacked in relays; aircraft and heavy guns ploughed the diamond-shaped position over and over. The fortress held for sixteen full days, tying down half of Rommel's force. On the night of 10–11 June, under orders, Koenig led his brigade out, and some 2,700 men broke through the lanes of their own minefields.

The photograph was taken by Leonard Chetwyn of the British No. 1 Army Film and Photo Section; the Imperial War Museum's original caption dates it to 12 June 1942 and describes Free French legionnaires springing from the desert to storm an enemy strongpoint — a scene from the closing phase of the battle. The legionnaires in the frame wear the iconic white sailor caps, khaki shirts and shorts, puttees wound down to below the knee; at the instant they rise, the whole line flattens into a forward-leaning diagonal. The next day Auchinleck, Commander-in-Chief Middle East, signalled that the United Nations should be filled with admiration and gratitude towards these French troops and their gallant General Koenig for what they had done at Bir Hakeim.

After Bir Hakeim, the claim that France still fights was no longer only a phrase on the radio. De Gaulle said the desert fortress showed the world that beyond the army that had signed Pétain's armistice there was another French army that had not surrendered. On the air of London and Cairo and over the BBC, Bir Hakeim became the first great battle-name of the Free French; after the war a bridge over the Seine in Paris was renamed the Pont de Bir-Hakeim, and the bronze plaque at its head records that at Bir Hakeim, from 27 May to 11 June 1942, the First Free French Brigade repelled the furious assaults of two enemy divisions and showed the world that France had never ceased fighting.

title: 舰艏刷漆
source: 英国帝国战争博物馆藏（A 1855），哈罗德·威廉·约翰·汤姆林（Harold William John Tomlin）摄于1940年，英国港口（普利茅斯）。画面要点：低角度仰视，自由法国水兵坐在悬挂于舷侧的吊板上，为大型驱逐舰『凯旋』号重漆舰艏，甲板上的战友凭舷俯望。
story: 1940年6月，法国败局已定，大型驱逐舰『凯旋』号为免落入德军之手，于21日驶离布雷斯特，抵达英国普利茅斯。7月3日，英国在『弹射行动』中接管了停泊在英国港口的法国军舰；8月28日，『凯旋』号移交自由法国海军，奥布瓦诺海军少校出任舰长——它是法国投降后第一批挂起洛林十字的军舰之一。水兵们没有军港，没有船坞，也没有整套的补给，却马上开始让这艘两千余吨的大军舰恢复战斗力：照片里，穿工装的自由法国水兵坐在舷外吊板上，悬在水面之上给舰艏重新涂漆，甲板上的战友凭舷看着他们。

9月至10月，舰上的后主炮换成了英制102毫米高射炮，装上英式声呐；10月23日，『凯旋』号重新服役，11月起编入第11护航大队，在克莱德湾加入北大西洋护航船队的护航序列。这艘舰此后转战三大洋：1941年取道巴拿马运河赴太平洋，驻新喀里多尼亚与澳大利亚；1943年在印度洋遭气旋重创；战后才回到法国。像所有自由法国军舰的舰艏一样，她的舷侧也漆着FNFL——自由法国海军——的字母，舰员臂章上的洛林十字与大不列颠的白色船艏徽并列。
照片的拍摄者哈罗德·汤姆林是英国《每日先驱报》出身的摄影记者，战时应征为皇家海军官方摄影师，帝国战争博物馆藏有他的大量作品。这张低角度仰拍的舰艏照，把一支流亡海军的全部处境都收进了画面：船还是法国的船，漆要自己刷，锚链上晾着的衣旗在海风里摆动——自由法国海军约五千余名水兵，就是从这样的吊板与漆桶之间重新出海的。

en.title: Painting the Bow
en.source: Imperial War Museum collection (A 1855); Harold William John Tomlin, taken in 1940 at a British port (Plymouth).
en.points: From a low upward angle, Free French sailors sit on staging rigged outboard of the ship's side, repainting the bow of the large destroyer Triomphant; shipmates lean over the rail on the deck above.
story: By June 1940 France's defeat was settled, and on the 21st the large destroyer Triomphant left Brest rather than fall into German hands, arriving at Plymouth in England. On 3 July, in Operation Catapult, Britain took over the French warships lying in her ports; on 28 August Triomphant was handed to the Free French Naval Forces, with Commander Auboyneau taking charge of her — she was among the first ships to raise the Cross of Lorraine after France's surrender. Her sailors had no naval base, no dockyard and no full system of supply, and they set about restoring this two-thousand-ton warship to fighting condition at once: in the photograph, Free French sailors in working dress sit on staging hung out over the side, suspended above the water as they repaint the bow, watched by shipmates leaning over the deck.

From September into October the ship's after main gun was exchanged for a British 102 mm anti-aircraft gun and British sonar was fitted; Triomphant recommissioned on 23 October, and from November she joined the 11th Escort Group on the North Atlantic convoy runs out of the Clyde. She went on to fight across three oceans: in 1941 she passed through the Panama Canal into the Pacific and served off New Caledonia and Australia; in 1943 she was badly damaged by a cyclone in the Indian Ocean; she returned to France only after the war. Like the bows of all Free French warships, her side carried the painted letters FNFL — Free French Naval Forces — and the Cross of Lorraine on her crew's sleeve patches stood alongside Britain's white bow badge.

The photographer, Harold Tomlin, came to the war from the Daily Herald as a press photographer and was commissioned into the Royal Navy's official photographic service; the Imperial War Museum holds a large body of his work. This low-angle view of a bow gathers the whole situation of a navy in exile into one frame: the ship is still French, the paint has to be laid on by her own crew, and clothing hung to dry along the anchor chain sways in the sea wind — the roughly five thousand sailors of the Free French Naval Forces put back to sea from between staging planks and paint buckets like these.

title: 伞兵与抵抗者
source: 美国陆军通信兵官方照片（下诺曼底大区与美国国家档案馆合作档案，编号 p012904），摄于1944年6月诺曼底。画面要点：近景，一名戴网罩钢盔的美军空降兵胸前挂着望远镜、叼着香烟，正听两名平民装束的法国抵抗组织成员讲述敌情。
story: 1944年6月6日凌晨，美军第82与第101空降师两万余人散落在科唐坦半岛的树篱田与沼泽之间。落地即集结的伞兵最先遇到的向导，往往就是当地农民与抵抗组织的成员：谁家谷仓里藏着德军哨所，哪条白杨道布雷，教堂钟楼上的机枪朝哪边打——这些情报决定着一支孤军的生死。英国特别行动执行署通过伦敦的内地军指挥部，早在登陆前就以BBC personal messages（个人消息）的密语通知各地抵抗组织实施『绿色计划』『海龟计划』等破坏任务，铁路、电话线与公路在6月6日前后被切断五百余处。美国陆军通信兵的摄影师在诺曼底拍下了这样一幕：一名伞兵叼着烟，胸前挂着望远镜，听两名头戴鸭舌帽与贝雷帽的抵抗者讲话。
照片流传的说明写作『诺曼底战役，1944年夏。法国抵抗组织成员与空降兵讨论形势』，英文维基百科的诺曼底登陆条目采用它作为抵抗组织与第82空降师会合的配图，原始档案存于下诺曼底大区与美国国家档案馆的合作影像库。画面里三个人的距离不过一米：军装与便装，枪与烟，伞降服上的快拆扣与农家的粗呢帽——两个世界在一块田埂上交换彼此知道的德军位置。
对散落各处的伞兵来说，抵抗者是眼睛和耳朵；对等待了四年的抵抗者来说，这些从天而降的士兵是兑现的承诺。在随后七个星期的诺曼底消耗战里，这种田间的合作不断扩大，到8月巴黎起义时，内地军已经能以旅为单位配属正规军作战。这张近景照片，是那部大机器最早也最小的一枚齿轮。

en.title: Paratroopers and the Resistance
en.source: Official U.S. Army Signal Corps photograph (joint archive of the Basse-Normandie region and the U.S. National Archives, no. p012904), taken in June 1944 in Normandy.
en.points: In close view, a U.S. airborne trooper in a net-covered helmet, binoculars at his chest and a cigarette in his mouth, listens while two Frenchmen in civilian clothes, members of the Resistance, describe the enemy situation.
story: In the early hours of 6 June 1944, more than twenty thousand men of the U.S. 82nd and 101st Airborne Divisions were scattered across the hedgerow fields and marshes of the Cotentin peninsula. The first guides the paratroopers met after landing were often local farmers and men of the Resistance: which barn hid a German post, which poplar-lined lane was mined, which way the machine gun in the church tower pointed — such intelligence decided whether an isolated unit lived. Through the FFI headquarters in London, the Special Operations Executive had already alerted the Resistance networks before the landings with the coded personal messages of the BBC, setting sabotage plans such as Plan Vert and Plan Tortue in motion; more than five hundred cuts fell on railways, telephone lines and roads around 6 June. A Signal Corps photographer in Normandy caught one such scene: a paratrooper with a cigarette, binoculars at his chest, listening to two Resistance men, one in a flat cap, one in a beret.

The caption that has circulated with the photograph reads: Normandy campaign, summer 1944 — French Resistance members discuss the situation with a paratrooper. The English Wikipedia article on the Normandy landings uses it for the meeting of the Resistance and the 82nd Airborne Division, and the original print sits in the joint image archive of the Basse-Normandie region and the U.S. National Archives. The three men in the frame stand barely a metre apart: uniform and civilian clothes, gun and cigarette, the quick-release fasteners of a jump jacket and a farmer's rough felt hat — two worlds trading what each knew of the German positions across a field bank.

For paratroopers scattered across the country, the Resistance were eyes and ears; for resisters who had waited four years, these soldiers out of the sky were a promise kept. Through the seven weeks of attrition that followed in Normandy, this cooperation in the fields kept widening, until by the Paris uprising of August the FFI could fight alongside regular troops at brigade strength. This close-up photograph is the earliest and smallest cog in that vast machine.

title: 卡瓦莱尔海滩
source: 美国国家档案馆藏照片（摄影师不详），摄于1944年8月18日，法国瓦尔省卡瓦莱尔（Cavalaire）海滩。画面要点：登陆后的海滩上，第18塞内加尔步兵团支部的一个排在队列里待命，钢盔与全套装具齐整，背景海面上运输舰与驳船络绎，远山朦胧。
story: 1944年8月15日，盟军在法国南部普罗旺斯发起『龙骑兵行动』，美军三个师在圣特罗佩至戛纳之间上岸；随后，德·拉特尔·德·塔西尼指挥的法国陆军B军——法国光复本土的主力——陆续从这里踏上国土。8月16日至18日，法属殖民地部队在卡瓦莱尔海湾登陆：马尼昂将军的第9殖民地步兵师在这里卸载，同期登岸的还有第18塞内加尔步兵团——1943年6月在达喀尔重建、先在科西嘉与厄尔巴岛作战的这支部队，将一路打到土伦和马赛城下。照片记录的正是8月18日卡瓦莱尔滩头的一个连队：钢盔下是来自塞内加尔、马里、布基纳法索的面孔，身后海面上，运输舰、驳船与登陆艇一直排到海平线。
第二次世界大战的法国军队里，约三十万殖民地士兵从1940年打到1945年，法国人叫他们『塞内加尔步枪兵』（tirailleurs sénégalais），尽管他们来自整个法属西非。1940年的战场上有一万名黑人士兵阵亡；1944年，从普罗旺斯上岸的法国部队约半数来自旧殖民地——土伦、马赛、里昂、阿尔萨斯，一路都有他们的纵队。照片里这支顶着钢盔在滩头列队的队伍，装备已是美式，军旗仍然是法国的。
11月至12月，这些部队将在阿尔萨斯与孚日山区迎来最冷的战役；而由于战后法军以『漂白』为名的整编，大多数塞内加尔步枪兵在1944年秋冬即被替换复员。卡瓦莱尔滩头的这个上午，因此成了他们与法国最贴近的一刻之一：脚下的沙子、身后的军舰与头顶的钢盔，都在说同一句话——我们是来解放法国的。

en.title: Cavalaire Beach
en.source: U.S. National Archives photograph (photographer unknown), taken on 18 August 1944 on the beach at Cavalaire, Var department, France.
en.points: On the beach after the landing, a platoon of a detachment of the 18th Senegalese Tirailleurs Regiment waits in formed ranks, helmets and full equipment in order; behind them transports and barges thread the sea, the far hills hazy.
story: On 15 August 1944 the Allies landed in Provence in southern France in Operation Dragoon, three U.S. divisions coming ashore between Saint-Tropez and Cannes; after them came French Army B under de Lattre de Tassigny — the main force of France's own liberation — stepping back onto national soil. From 16 to 18 August the colonial units of that army landed in the bay of Cavalaire: General Magnan's 9th Colonial Infantry Division unloaded here, and landing at the same time was the 18th Senegalese Tirailleurs Regiment — rebuilt at Dakar in June 1943 and first blooded in Corsica and on Elba — a regiment that would fight its way to Toulon and to the walls of Marseille. The photograph records a company on the Cavalaire beachhead on 18 August: under the steel helmets are faces from Senegal, Mali and Burkina Faso, and behind them transports, barges and landing craft stretch away to the horizon.

In the French army of the Second World War, some three hundred thousand colonial soldiers served from 1940 to 1945; the French called them tirailleurs sénégalais, Senegalese riflemen, though they came from all of French West Africa. Ten thousand Black soldiers fell in the fighting of 1940; in 1944 roughly half the French force that landed in Provence came from the old colonies — Toulon, Marseille, Lyon, Alsace: their columns marched every stage of the way. The unit standing in ranks on this beach is equipped on the American pattern, but the flag it follows is still the flag of France.

In November and December these units would meet their coldest campaign in Alsace and the Vosges; and under the postwar reorganisation the French army called blanchiment, the whitening of the ranks, most of the Senegalese tirailleurs were replaced and demobilised as early as the autumn and winter of 1944. This morning on the Cavalaire beachhead was therefore one of their closest moments with France: the sand underfoot, the warships behind, the helmets overhead all said one thing — we have come to liberate France.

title: 协和广场的枪声
source: 美国陆军通信兵官方照片，美国国家档案馆藏（National Archives Identifier 531206，战争与冲突编号 1057），摄影师不详，摄于1944年8月26日，巴黎协和广场。画面要点：庆祝人群中狙击手突然开火，人群在铁丝网拒马间四散卧倒，一名警察推着自行车伏低，穿花裙的妇人疾步穿行。
story: 1944年8月26日下午，巴黎解放的次日，戴高乐率游行队伍从凯旋门下行香榭丽舍大街，穿过协和广场前往市政厅与圣母院——从抵抗组织领导到巴黎市民，数十万人挤满了这条路线。但城里的枪声并没有停：少数拒不投降的德军狙击手与民兵仍盘踞在几座建筑里。当人群涌过协和广场开阔的石面时，枪响了。通信兵摄影师拍下的这一刻后来入藏美国国家档案馆，原始说明写着：『庆祝盟军进入巴黎的巴黎人群，在一名狙击手从协和广场一座建筑里向他们开火时四散寻找掩护。尽管德军已投降这座城市，小股狙击手仍在负隅顽抗。1944年8月26日。』

画面里，庆祝在一秒钟内变成了求生：铁丝网拒马翻倒在地，人群齐刷刷伏低，有人扑进拒马背后，有人贴着路灯柱蹲下，一名警察推着自行车伏在车后，一名穿花裙的妇人反而站起身快步穿过空地——每个人都在按自己的本能行动。当天，同样的枪声两次打断戴高乐的路线：在协和广场，在圣母院广场，子弹擦着石面弹跳。卡纳瓦莱博物馆藏有同一时刻、同一地点的另一张照片，署名是抵抗组织的摄影师约瑟夫·斯坦纳（化名安德烈），可与此图互证。
这是巴黎解放日最著名的一张照片之一：胜利与危险同框，节日被压缩成一条本能的弧线。狙击手的枪声零星持续到8月末，巴黎的大游行却在那天下午照常走完了全程——对刚刚重获自由的巴黎人来说，卧倒之后爬起来，庆祝还要继续。

en.title: Sniper Fire at the Concorde
en.source: Official U.S. Army Signal Corps photograph, U.S. National Archives (National Archives Identifier 531206, War & Conflict no. 1057), photographer unknown, taken on 26 August 1944 at the Place de la Concorde, Paris.
en.points: Sniper fire breaks out without warning in the celebrating crowd; people scatter and drop among the barbed-wire hedgehogs, a policeman crouches low behind his bicycle, and a woman in a flowered dress hurries across the open ground.
story: On the afternoon of 26 August 1944, the day after the liberation of Paris, de Gaulle led the march down the Champs-Élysées from the Arc de Triomphe, across the Place de la Concorde, toward the Hôtel de Ville and Notre-Dame — hundreds of thousands, from Resistance leaders to ordinary Parisians, packed the route. But the sound of gunfire in the city had not stopped: a handful of German snipers and militiamen who refused to surrender still held out in buildings here and there. As the crowd poured over the Concorde's open stone, the shots came. The moment caught by a Signal Corps photographer entered the U.S. National Archives with the original caption: Parisians celebrating the Allied entry into Paris scatter for cover as a sniper fires on them from a building on the Place de la Concorde; although the Germans had surrendered the city, small bands of snipers still resisted. 26 August 1944.

In the frame, celebration turns into survival within a second: barbed-wire hedgehogs lie knocked over, the crowd drops as one, some throw themselves behind the obstacles, some crouch at the foot of lampposts, a policeman crouches low behind his bicycle, and a woman in a flowered dress instead gets up and strides across the open ground — everyone acting on instinct alone. That day the same gunfire twice broke into de Gaulle's route: at the Concorde, and on the square before Notre-Dame, bullets skipping off the stone. The Musée Carnavalet holds another photograph of the same moment at the same place, credited to the Resistance photographer Joseph Steiner, alias André, which corroborates this one.

This is among the best-known photographs of the liberation of Paris: victory and danger share one frame, the festival compressed into a single reflexive arc. Sniper fire continued in bursts to the end of August, yet the great march that afternoon completed its course — for Parisians just given back their freedom, you picked yourself up after ducking, and went on celebrating.

title: 马赛烧旗
source: 美国陆军通信兵官方照片（编号 SC 194304，美国国家档案馆藏），摄于1944年8月28日，马赛。画面要点：人群展开一面从警察局大楼上取下的纳粹党旗，中央一名穿浅色衬衫的男子蹲身点火，周围水兵、钢盔士兵与欢呼的市民围成一圈。
story: 马赛的解放和巴黎几乎同步：8月21日战斗打响，抵抗组织先期占领了警察局，德蒙萨贝特将军的第3阿尔及利亚步兵师与内地军部队在老港的街巷里逐垒争夺，海军的炮口贴着圣尼古拉堡轰击。8月27日20时，马赛德军守将舍费尔签署投降书，28日15时投降生效——一万一千余名德军放下武器，比原计划提前了近一个月。当天，人们在欢呼声中把一直飘在警察局大楼上的那面纳粹旗扯了下来。美国陆军通信兵摄影师拍下的人群，后来以编号SC 194304入藏美国国家档案馆，美国大屠杀纪念馆也收藏了同一张：『庆祝马赛解放的人群焚烧那面一直飘扬在警察局大楼上的纳粹旗。1944年8月28日。』

照片中央，一名穿浅色衬衫的男子蹲下身，把火凑近摊开的旗角，四周的人把手举过头顶欢呼——戴白帽的水兵、便装的青年、戴美式钢盔的法军士兵，还有扒着窗台的孩子们。四年前，就在同一座港口，另一面旗帜曾让一位中年人当众落泪：1940年9月，法国陆军的团旗依照停战条款被装船运往北非，本组另一张照片《流泪的法国人》定格的正是那个马赛的上午。1944年8月的这个下午，马赛人烧掉的是敌国的旗——一面当年被强行收走的荣誉之旗与一面被当众焚毁的占领之旗，隔着四年，在这座地中海大港完成了一次对答。
解放次日，德·拉特尔·德·塔西尼与内政委员阿斯提耶·德·拉·维热里在老港检阅了部队。马赛港随即成为盟军在欧洲最重要的补给口岸——到1944年底，经由这座港口上岸的物资已占盟军在欧洲大陆补给量的三分之一。而这张烧旗的照片，被历史选作了那场解放的句读。

en.title: Burning the Flag in Marseille
en.source: Official U.S. Army Signal Corps photograph (no. SC 194304, U.S. National Archives), taken on 28 August 1944 in Marseille.
en.points: A crowd spreads out a Nazi party flag taken down from the police headquarters building; at the centre a man in a light-coloured shirt crouches to set it alight, ringed by sailors, helmeted soldiers and cheering townspeople.
story: Marseille's liberation ran almost in step with Paris's: the fighting opened on 21 August, the Resistance seized the police headquarters early on, General de Monsabert's 3rd Algerian Infantry Division and FFI troops fought stronghold by stronghold through the lanes of the old port, and the guns of the fleet fired point-blank at Fort Saint-Nicolas. At 20:00 on 27 August the German commander of Marseille, Schaefer, signed the capitulation, which took effect at 15:00 on the 28th — more than eleven thousand Germans laid down their arms, nearly a month ahead of the original plan. That day, amid the cheering, the Nazi flag that had flown over the police headquarters was torn down. The crowd a U.S. Army Signal Corps photographer shot entered the National Archives as SC 194304; the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum holds the same photograph under the caption: crowds celebrating the liberation of Marseille burn the Nazi flag that had flown over the police headquarters, 28 August 1944.

At the centre of the frame a man in a light-coloured shirt crouches and brings his fire to the spread corner of the flag, and around him hands go up in cheers — sailors in white caps, young men in civilian clothes, French soldiers in American helmets, children hanging from the window sills. Four years earlier, at this same port, another flag had made a middle-aged man weep in the open street: in September 1940 the regimental colours of the French army were shipped away to North Africa under the armistice terms, and another photograph in this series, The Weeping Frenchman, froze that Marseille morning. On this August afternoon of 1944 the people of Marseille burned the flag of the enemy state — a colour of honour taken away by force, and an occupier's flag burned in public, four years apart, answered one another in this great Mediterranean port.

The day after the liberation, de Lattre de Tassigny and Interior Commissioner Astier de la Vigerie reviewed troops at the old port. The port of Marseille at once became the most important supply gateway of the Allies in Europe — by the end of 1944, tonnage landed there made up a third of Allied supply on the continent. And this photograph of the burning flag became the full stop history set against that liberation.

title: 西线重炮
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏(Bild 101I-054-1527-14),第670战地宣传连摄影师鲍尔(Bauer)摄于1940年5月法国战役期间。画面要点:白桦林间的炮位上,炮手们正为15厘米sFH 18重榴弹炮传运炮弹,长身管斜指天空,前景一名挽袖士兵横抱两枚弹体弯腰疾走,右侧堆着弹药箱与草筐。
story: 1940年5月,法国北部的林间炮位:第670战地宣传连的摄影师鲍尔拍下了这门sFH 18重榴弹炮装填的瞬间。sFH 18(schwere Feldhaubitze 18)是二战德军师属炮兵的主力重炮,口径15厘米,射程13公里余,40余公斤的弹体与发射药分两次装填——照片里赤膊上阵的炮手们,正在树影与尘土之间重复这套笨重而讲究节奏的动作。
5月10日,德军穿越阿登绕过马其诺防线突入法国,装甲集群直扑英吉利海峡把联军主力截成两段;英军从敦刻尔克丢下重装备撤回本土,6月14日巴黎不设防开城,6月22日法国在贡比涅森林签署停战协定——六个星期,一个号称欧洲陆军最强的国度战败。这种一边倒的胜利让『闪电战』三个字此后数年始终笼罩在德军头顶,也把西线的战火熄成了长达四年的占领与对峙。

这帧照片里没有冲锋与爆炸,只有一门炮与一班人的日常:传弹、开闩、装填、复进。德军战地宣传连(Propagandakompanie)在战争年代向前线派驻了数以万计的官兵摄影师,他们生产的影像既服务于当时的报纸与新闻片,战后也成为联邦档案馆里研究这场战争最庞大的影像来源之一——照片里这些来不及留下姓名的炮手,是千千万万个炮班的缩影:法国的胜利顶点之上,他们中的多数人还不知道,自己将与这门炮一起,一路打到1945年。

en.title: Heavy Guns on the Western Front
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 101I-054-1527-14; photographer Bauer of Propaganda Company 670, taken in May 1940 during the Battle of France.
en.points: At a gun position among birch trees the gunners pass shells up to a 15 cm sFH 18 heavy field howitzer, its long barrel slanted at the sky; in the foreground a soldier with rolled-up sleeves bends under two shell bodies carried in his arms and hurries forward, ammunition boxes and wicker baskets stacked at the right.
story: A gun position in the woods of northern France, May 1940: Bauer, photographer of Propaganda Company 670, caught the loading of this sFH 18 heavy howitzer at the instant. The sFH 18 (schwere Feldhaubitze 18) was the principal heavy gun of the German divisional artillery of the Second World War: 15 cm calibre, a range of over thirteen kilometres, its forty-odd-kilogram shell and propellant charge loaded in two separate movements — in the photograph, gunners stripped to the waist repeat that clumsy, rhythm-bound drill between tree-shadow and dust.

On 10 May the German army came through the Ardennes, turned the Maginot Line and broke into France; the armoured groups drove for the English Channel and cut the Allied main force in two. The British left their heavy equipment behind at Dunkirk and came home; Paris fell open and undefended on 14 June; on 22 June France signed the armistice in the forest of Compiègne — six weeks, and the state reputed to have the strongest army in Europe was beaten. A victory so one-sided kept the word Blitzkrieg over the German army for years afterwards, and pressed the war in the west down into four years of occupation and standoff.

There is no charge and no explosion in this frame, only the daily round of one gun and its crew: passing shells, opening the breech, loading, running back. The German propaganda companies (Propagandakompanien) sent tens of thousands of soldier-photographers to the front during the war years; the images they made fed the newspapers and newsreels of their day and, after the war, became one of the largest photographic sources for the study of the war in the Federal Archives — the gunners in the picture, too hurried to leave their names, stand for the tens of thousands of gun crews like them: at the high-water mark of the victory in France, most of them did not yet know that they and this gun would go on marching until 1945.

title: 雪地里的斯图卡
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏(Bild 101I-392-1334-04),战地摄影师万德雷尔(Wanderer, W.)摄于1941年12月22日,苏德前线一处雪原野战机场。画面要点:一架换装雪橇起落架的Ju 87俯冲轰炸机敞开发动机整流罩检修,军官与白色冬季伪装服的地勤立在机头旁,木梯搭上机身。
story: 1941年12月22日,苏德前线,积雪没踝的野战机场:一架Ju 87斯图卡俯冲轰炸机把主轮换成了雪橇,机修兵们敞开发动机整流罩检修——气温跌到零下三四十度的机场上,轮式起落架一落地就会陷进雪洞里折断,每一架还能飞的飞机都得靠地勤用双手从寒夜里抠出来。摄影师万德雷尔按下的这一帧里,雪原与白色天空在远处连成一线。
这年12月5日,苏军在莫斯科城下发起全线反攻,德军自开战以来第一次被迫后撤。1941年的冬天来得又早又狠:坦克发动机要在车底生火烘烤才能启动,机枪润滑油冻成糊,士兵的夏季制服里塞着缴获的棉衣和报纸。飞机的处境最直接——没有保温机库,地勤只能在雪地里拆装发动机、灌热油、摇启动摇柄,照片里那副雪橇,就是1941至42年之交的冬天在东线机场上急就章的土办法之一。
斯图卡曾是闪电战的声音符号:1939年波兰、1940年法国、1941年巴尔干与克里特,耶利哥号角般的俯冲啸声是德国空军最出名的名片;但到1941年冬,面对战斗机的拦截与漫长战线上的消耗,它的黄金年代已经过去。照片里检修它的人没有留下姓名——一场战争的走向,往往就悬在这样一些不起眼的机务日常上:发动机能否在零下四十度再启动一次,决定了第二天清晨还有没有飞机起飞。

en.title: Stuka in the Snow
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 101I-392-1334-04; war photographer Wanderer, W., taken on 22 December 1941 at a snow-covered forward airfield on the German-Soviet front.
en.points: A Ju 87 dive bomber with its main wheels exchanged for skis stands with the engine cowling open for maintenance; officers and ground crew in white winter camouflage suits stand by the nose, a wooden ladder set against the fuselage.
story: 22 December 1941, the German-Soviet front, a forward airfield ankle-deep in snow: a Ju 87 Stuka dive bomber has had its wheels swapped for skis, and the mechanics work behind an opened engine cowling — on airfields where the temperature fell to thirty and forty below, wheeled undercarriage broke through into snow hollows the moment it touched down, and every aircraft still able to fly was clawed back out of the cold nights by the ground crews' bare hands. In this one frame of the photographer Wanderer's, snowfield and white sky run together into a single line in the distance.

On 5 December that year the Soviet army had opened its counter-offensive before Moscow, and for the first time since the campaign began the German army was forced back. The winter of 1941 came early and hard: tank engines had to be coaxed alive with fires lit under the hulls, machine-gun oil froze to paste, soldiers packed captured padded jackets and newspaper into their summer uniforms. The aircraft suffered most directly — with no heated hangars, ground crews stripped and rebuilt engines in the open snow, poured warm oil and swung the starting handles by hand; the skis in this photograph were one of the rough-and-ready answers the winter of 1941–42 forced on the airfields of the East.

The Stuka had been the voice of Blitzkrieg: over Poland in 1939, France in 1940, the Balkans and Crete in 1941, its Jericho-trumpet howl in the dive was the most famous calling card of the Luftwaffe; but by the winter of 1941, against fighter interception and the attrition of a lengthening front, its golden age was already past. The men servicing it in the photograph left no names — the course of a war often hung on maintenance days as unremarkable as this one: whether an engine could be brought to life once more at minus forty decided whether any aircraft took off the next morning.

title: 北非出击前
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏(Bild 101I-428-0485-13A),空军第7战地宣传连摄影师洛斯尼策(Loßnitzer)摄于1941年,北非。画面要点:一架沙色迷彩的Bf 109战斗机旁,穿白色救生背心的飞行员弯腰紧靴整装,地勤倚在白色机身机号旁,背后是野战机场的弯顶机库。
story: 1941年,北非:出击之前,一名飞行员在座舱下方弯腰紧好飞行靴,白色救生背心套在飞行服外——在地中海上空执行任务,一旦跳伞落水,这件救生背心就是全部的生还指望;一旁的地勤穿着连体工装,倚着画有巨大白色机号的机身。这架Bf 109(梅塞施密特Me 109)涂着沙漠底色上的云斑迷彩,用来在沙漠上空打散轮廓。空军第7宣传连的洛斯尼策在野战机场上拍下了这个安静的出发时刻。

1941年2月,德意非洲军团的先头部队在的黎波里登陆,隆美尔不等部队到齐就发起反攻,把战线一路推向埃及边境。为这支陆军撑起天空的是以第27战斗机联队为代表的Bf 109部队:扫射、拦截、为俯冲轰炸机开路,还要分出大批架次去封锁马耳他——这座英军据点卡在轴心国地中海航线的咽喉上,双方围绕它缠斗两年。北非的作战环境对所有装备都苛刻:细沙钻进发动机与枪机,正午座舱里能到五十度,地勤每天的头等大事是赶在沙尘吞掉飞机之前把它抢修好。
照片里的飞行员与地勤都没有留下姓名,这正是大多数出击的样子:一次平凡得不能再平凡的起飞准备,战斗机后面跟着的是一班完全信任它的人。北非的空战打到1943年5月,轴心国部队在突尼斯集体投降,约25万人被俘——那片沙漠迷彩与白色机号,最终都消失在撤退与被俘的人潮里。这帧出击前的定格,是北非战役尚在势头上时,德军飞行员日常的一瞬。

en.title: Before the Sortie, North Africa
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 101I-428-0485-13A; photographer Loßnitzer of Luftwaffe Propaganda Company 7, taken in 1941 in North Africa.
en.points: Beside a sand-coloured Bf 109 fighter, a pilot wearing a white life vest bends to tighten his flying boots; a ground-crew man leans against the fuselage by the large white aircraft number, and behind rise the curved roofs of a forward airfield's hangars.
story: North Africa, 1941: before the sortie, a pilot bends below the cockpit to pull his flying boots tight, a white life vest over his flying suit — on missions flown over the Mediterranean, if he came down in the sea, that vest was the whole of his hope of survival; beside him a ground-crew man in overalls leans against the fuselage painted with its great white number. This Bf 109 (Messerschmitt Me 109) wears cloud-blotch camouflage over a desert base, laid on to break up its outline against the sand. Loßnitzer of Luftwaffe Propaganda Company 7 caught this quiet moment of departure on a forward airfield.

In February 1941 the leading units of the German-Italian Afrika Korps landed at Tripoli, and Rommel attacked before his force had fully arrived, driving the line all the way to the Egyptian frontier. Holding the sky above this army were the Bf 109 wings, above all Jagdgeschwader 27: strafing, interception, opening the way for the dive bombers — and spending whole blocks of sorties on the blockade of Malta, the British stronghold sitting on the throat of the Axis sea route through the Mediterranean, fought over by both sides for two years. The North African environment spared no equipment: fine sand worked into engines and gun mechanisms, cockpit temperatures at midday could reach fifty degrees, and each day the ground crews' first task was to win the aircraft back before the dust swallowed them.

Neither the pilot nor the ground-crew man in the photograph left a name, and that is what most sorties looked like: a take-off preparation ordinary past describing, and behind the fighter a crew of men who trusted it without reserve. The air war in North Africa ran on to May 1943, when the Axis forces in Tunisia surrendered together and some 250,000 men went into captivity — that desert camouflage and those white aircraft numbers alike vanished into the crowds of the retreat and the prisoner columns. This frozen moment before a sortie is one instant out of the German pilots' daily round, taken while the North African campaign still ran with them.

title: U-552号进港
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏(Bild 101II-MW-3676-28),战地记者洛塔尔-京特·布赫海姆(Lothar-Günther Buchheim)摄于1941年10月6日,法国圣纳泽尔潜艇基地。画面要点:U-552号艇驶入港内,艇长埃里希·托普(右)白色艇长帽、胸前挂双筒望远镜叉腰立于指挥塔上,军官与艇员在旁,桅索上挂着一串凯旋三角旗。
story: 1941年10月6日,法国大西洋岸的圣纳泽尔:VIIC型潜艇U-552号缓缓驶入卢瓦尔河口,桅索上飘着一串三角旗——按潜艇部队的惯例,那是这一趟巡逻的战果计数。指挥塔上,艇长埃里希·托普戴着白色艇长帽、胸前挂双筒望远镜叉腰而立,军官与艇员们围在塔上,被摄下了凯旋入港的一刻。按下快门的战地记者洛塔尔-京特·布赫海姆,当时刚随U-96号艇结束一次大西洋巡逻返港。

U-552号绰号『红魔』,是德国潜艇部队战绩最高的艇之一,整场战争共击沉舰船35艘。托普1941年6月获颁骑士十字勋章,此后一路升任支队指挥官,终战时位列德国潜艇王牌第三。这张照片拍下三周之后的10月31日,U-552号在冰岛以南击沉美国驱逐舰『鲁本·詹姆斯』号——那是美国海军在二战中损失的第一艘军舰,约百名舰员阵亡,而那时美国还没有参战。U-552号一直服役到战争末尾,1945年5月5日为免被俘在威廉港自沉。
圣纳泽尔是德国潜艇在大西洋岸最大的基地之一,钢筋混凝土的潜艇掩体从1941年起一直修到战争结束,盟军的炸弹始终没能奈何它。至于布赫海姆:1941年秋他随U-96号艇出海,一路画速写、拍下数千张照片,三十多年后写成长篇小说《从海底出击》,1981年由沃尔夫冈·彼得森搬上银幕,成为最著名的潜艇电影——这张入港照,正是那段亲历影像里的一帧。

en.title: U-552 Entering Port
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 101II-MW-3676-28; war correspondent Lothar-Günther Buchheim, taken on 6 October 1941 at the U-boat base of Saint-Nazaire, France.
en.points: The U-boat U-552 comes into harbour; her commander Erich Topp (at right) stands on the conning tower in the white commander's cap, binoculars at his chest and hands on hips, with officers and crew about him and a string of victory pennants flying from the mast rigging.
story: 6 October 1941, Saint-Nazaire on the French Atlantic coast: the Type VIIC boat U-552 slides slowly into the Loire estuary, a string of pennants at her rigging — by the custom of the U-boat service, the tally of this patrol's sinkings. On the conning tower her commander, Erich Topp, stands in the white commander's cap, binoculars at his chest, fists on hips, officers and crew gathered on the tower: the moment of a victorious homecoming, put on film by the war correspondent Lothar-Günther Buchheim, who had himself just come back to port from an Atlantic patrol aboard U-96.

U-552, nicknamed the Red Devil, was one of the highest-scoring boats of the U-boat arm, sinking 35 ships over the course of the war. Topp received the Knight's Cross in June 1941, went on to command a flotilla, and ended the war third among Germany's U-boat aces. Three weeks after this photograph, on 31 October, U-552 sank the American destroyer Reuben James south of Iceland — the first warship the United States Navy lost in the Second World War, with about a hundred of her people killed, at a time when the United States was not yet at war. U-552 served to the very end, scuttled at Wilhelmshaven on 5 May 1945 to keep out of enemy hands.

Saint-Nazaire was among the largest of the German U-boat bases on the Atlantic; its reinforced-concrete pens rose from 1941 until the end of the war, and the Allies' bombs never mastered them. As for Buchheim: in the autumn of 1941 he sailed on U-96, sketching and taking thousands of photographs, and more than thirty years later wrote the novel Das Boot, brought to the screen by Wolfgang Petersen in 1981 as the most famous of submarine films — this photograph of a boat entering harbour is one frame out of that first-hand record.

title: 虎式装弹
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏(Bild 183-J14931),战地摄影师罗滕施泰纳(Rottensteiner)摄于1943年7月,别尔哥罗德近郊,库尔斯克会战期间;舍尔图片社通稿编号3787-43。画面要点:虎式重型坦克炮塔侧甲上码着88毫米炮弹,两名乘员合力传递一发弹,粗大的炮管探出画面右缘。
story: 1943年7月,别尔哥罗德近郊:库尔斯克突出部南翼,一辆虎式重型坦克停在集结地里补充弹药,两名车组乘员站在炮塔侧甲上合力传递一发88毫米炮弹,弹体一发发码放在甲板上,旁边放着备用履带与伪装枝叶。战地摄影师罗滕施泰纳拍下的这一幕,由舍尔图片社以3787-43的编号向报章发稿。
虎式(Pz.Kpfw. VI Tiger I)是德国在战争中期投入的重型坦克:57吨,正面装甲100毫米,主炮是从高射炮移植的88毫米炮,足以在两千米外击穿对手;1942年秋它先后在列宁格勒郊外与突尼斯首次参战。1943年7月5日,德军发动『城堡行动』,从库尔斯克突出部南北两面向心夹击,别尔哥罗德方向是南翼的进攻轴线,虎式坦克营被当作砸开苏军防御纵深的重锤用在这个方向上。
这场攻势只持续了一个多星期:南翼在普罗霍罗夫卡一带与苏军坦克部队绞杀到7月中旬,7月10日盟军在西西里登陆,希特勒下令抽兵南援,『城堡』半途而废;8月初苏军转入反攻,别尔哥罗德与哈尔科夫相继易手。照片里这几发码上炮塔的炮弹,因此落在整场攻势的顶点上——库尔斯克之后,德军在东线再也没有发起过战略进攻。

en.title: Loading the Tiger
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 183-J14931; war photographer Rottensteiner, taken in July 1943 near Belgorod during the Battle of Kursk; Scherl picture service, wire photo no. 3787-43.
en.points: 88 mm shells are stacked on the turret side plate of a Tiger heavy tank while two crew members together pass up a further round; the massive gun barrel reaches out past the right edge of the frame.
story: July 1943, near Belgorod: on the southern face of the Kursk salient a Tiger heavy tank stands in a forward assembly area taking on ammunition; two crew men on the turret side plate together pass up an 88 mm shell, the rounds laid one by one on the armour deck, spare track links and camouflage branches beside them. The scene the war photographer Rottensteiner shot went out to the newspapers through the Scherl picture service under number 3787-43.

The Tiger (Pz.Kpfw. VI Tiger I) was the heavy tank Germany put into the field in the middle of the war: 57 tonnes, 100 mm of frontal armour, a main gun carried over from the 88 mm anti-aircraft gun and able to punch through its opponents at two thousand metres; it first fought in the autumn of 1942, outside Leningrad and in Tunisia. On 5 July 1943 the German army opened Operation Citadel, attacking inward from the north and south faces of the Kursk salient; the Belgorod sector was the axis of the southern drive, and the Tiger battalions were sent there as the heavy hammer to break the depth of the Soviet defences.

The offensive lasted scarcely a week and a half: on the southern face the fighting ground itself out in the tank melee around Prokhorovka into mid-July; the Allies landed in Sicily on 10 July, Hitler drew forces away to the south, and Citadel was left half-finished; in early August the Soviet army passed to the counter-offensive, and Belgorod and Kharkov changed hands in turn. The shells stacked on this turret therefore sit at the very crest of the offensive — after Kursk, the German army in the East never again opened a strategic offensive.

title: 前进观测哨
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏(Bild 146-1985-022-25),战地摄影师戈特特(Göttert)摄于1943年12月的东线,原始图注于1944年1月24日作为通稿发布。画面要点:一名炮兵前进观测员趴在田埂边的单兵掩体里举着野战电话听筒,身侧横着步枪、插着铁锹,前景是线拐与电话机包,背后一排落尽叶子的白桦。
story: 1943年12月的东线,雪覆的原野上:一名炮兵前进观测员趴在田埂边的单兵掩体里,钢盔压着絮棉的冬季军服,左手举着野战电话听筒,右手撑着冻土;掩体里横着步枪、插着铁锹,电话线从线拐一直铺向后方炮兵阵地。当年德军战时报道的原版图注这样写:『弹坑、步枪、铁锹和电话机,就是这位前进观测员的全部世界。』摄影师戈特特的这张照片于1944年1月24日发布。
前进观测员(vorgeschobener Beobachter)是炮兵的眼睛:炮兵部队把最冷静的人派到步兵战线前缘,他找到目标、算出方位,再用那部野战电话把口令报回阵地——整片战线上几百门炮的落点,就系在他这根细电线上。照片里的人属于『大德意志』装甲掷弹兵师,这支部队是陆军统帅部直接掌握的王牌,1943年冬天在第聂伯河湾的反击与堵口之间来回奔波,被当作东线中段的消防队使用。
拍下这张照片的冬天,东线大势已定:第聂伯河防线在1943年11月被苏军突破,基辅易手,德军一路退向1939年的旧边界。原版图注里那句修辞,今天读来更像谶语——照片里这个坑、一杆枪、一把锹和一部电话,就是1943年冬季一名普通德国炮兵观测员的全部战争;他朝着镜头露出的那点笑意,成了这张档案照里最有人味的一笔。

en.title: Forward Observer
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 146-1985-022-25; war photographer Göttert, taken in December 1943 on the Eastern Front; the original caption went out as a wire photo on 24 January 1944.
en.points: An artillery forward observer lies in a one-man foxhole at the edge of a field bank with the receiver of a field telephone at his ear; a rifle lies at his side and a spade stands stuck in the ground; in the foreground the wire reel and the telephone pack, behind him a row of leafless birches.
story: Eastern Front, December 1943, snow-covered open country: an artillery forward observer lies in a one-man foxhole at the edge of a field bank, steel helmet over a padded winter uniform, the field-telephone receiver in his left hand and his right hand braced against the frozen earth; a rifle lies in the foxhole, a spade stands in the ground, and the field wire runs off from the reel toward the gun positions behind. The original German wartime caption reads: shell hole, rifle, spade and telephone — that is the forward observer's whole world. The photograph by Göttert was released on 24 January 1944.

The forward observer (vorgeschobener Beobachter) was the eyes of the artillery: the batteries sent their calmest men to the forward edge of the infantry line, where he found the target, worked out the bearing, and read the fire orders back over the field telephone — where the shells of hundreds of guns along the whole front fell hung upon his one thin wire. The man in the photograph belonged to the Großdeutschland Panzergrenadier Division, an elite held directly under the Army High Command, which spent the winter of 1943 shuttling between counterattacks and stopgaps in the Dnieper bend — the fire brigade of the central sector.

By the winter this photograph was taken, the fate of the Eastern Front was already settled: the Dnieper line was broken in November 1943, Kiev changed hands, and the German army fell back toward the old borders of 1939. The rhetorical flourish of that original caption reads today almost as prophecy — this hole in the ground, one rifle, one spade and one telephone were the whole war of one ordinary German artillery observer in the winter of 1943; the small smile he turns toward the camera is the most human stroke in this archival photograph.

title: 人民冲锋
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏(Bild 146-1973-001-36),摄影师不详,1945年3月初摄于德国某城。画面要点:一名穿大衣便帽的人民冲锋队员单膝跪地试射『铁拳』反坦克火箭,发射的白烟罩过右半幅画面,身后围观者多为戴礼帽穿大衣的中老年男子,左缘立着一名制服少年。
story: 1945年3月初,德国本土某城:一名穿长大衣、戴软帽的中年男子单膝跪地,平举一枚『铁拳』反坦克火箭筒试射,发射药的白烟从筒口喷涌而出,翻卷成巨大的烟云罩过右半幅画面;身后围观的人们大多四五十岁上下,穿着日常的大衣与礼帽——他们不是军人,是人民冲锋队(Volkssturm)。联邦档案馆的原始说明只写了一句:『人民冲锋队在德国某城进行铁拳试射』,摄影师没有留下姓名。
人民冲锋队由希特勒在1944年9月25日下令组建:凡16至60岁、尚未服役的男性一律征入,由各行政区长官统领,武器、军服与训练全都严重不足。发给他们的主力武器就是铁拳——一根装着空心装药战斗部的廉价一次性发射筒,在30到60米射程上的破甲能力足以击穿任何一种盟军坦克,总产量以百万计;它不需要瞄准镜,也几乎不需要训练,教官们说得最多的一句话是:离敌人再近一点。
到1945年春,训练场上这些戴礼帽的男人和穿制服的少年,已经被推到了战争的最后一段:莱茵河上的雷马根桥3月7日失守,西线大门洞开;东线的奥德河防线4月被苏军碾过,柏林卫戍司令5月2日缴械,德国在5月8日签署无条件投降书。照片里的这次试射,是他们领到的全部战争——多数人从训练场直接走进了自己城市的街垒,很多人再没有回来。

en.title: The Volkssturm
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 146-1973-001-36; photographer unknown, taken in early March 1945 in a German town.
en.points: A Volkssturm man in overcoat and soft hat kneels on one knee to test-fire a Panzerfaust anti-tank launcher; the white smoke of the discharge washes over the right half of the frame, the onlookers behind him mostly middle-aged and elderly men in hats and coats, a uniformed boy standing at the left edge.
story: A German town, early March 1945: a middle-aged man in a long overcoat and a soft hat kneels on one knee and levels a Panzerfaust anti-tank launcher for a test shot; the white smoke of the propellant charge pours from the tube mouth and rolls up into a great cloud over the right half of the frame; the people watching behind are mostly in their forties and fifties, in everyday coats and felt hats — they are not soldiers, they are the Volkssturm. The Bundesarchiv's original caption says only that the Volkssturm is test-firing a Panzerfaust in a German town; the photographer left no name.

The Volkssturm was created by Hitler's order of 25 September 1944: every male from sixteen to sixty not already serving was conscripted, under the command of the regional party leaders, with weapons, uniforms and training all in desperately short supply. The main weapon issued them was the Panzerfaust — a cheap, single-shot tube throwing a shaped-charge warhead, whose armour penetration at thirty to sixty metres could go through any Allied tank; it wanted no gunsight and hardly any training, and the sentence the instructors repeated most was: get closer to the enemy. Production ran into the millions.

By the spring of 1945 the men in hats on this training ground and the boys in uniform had been pushed into the last stretch of the war: the Remagen bridge over the Rhine was lost on 7 March and the gate to the west stood open; on the east the Soviet army ground over the Oder line in April; the Berlin garrison laid down its arms on 2 May; Germany signed unconditional surrender on 8 May. The test-firing in this photograph was the whole of the war these men were given — most went straight from the training ground into the barricades of their own towns, and many never came back.

title: 但泽难民车队
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏(Bild 146-1996-028-36A),摄影师布里吉特·赫贝尔(Brigitte Höber)摄于1945年2月20日至21日,但泽(今格但斯克)近郊。画面要点:俯瞰街面,一驾双马板车满载被褥、提篮与妇孺沿街而行,车上人蜷缩在毯子下,右前景一个小小的女孩独立在路缘石上。
story: 1945年2月20日前后,但泽近郊:摄影师布里吉特·赫贝尔从街边高处俯瞰,拍下这支西行的难民车队——两匹挽马拉着满载的农用板车,被褥、提篮、草捆与锅盆在车板上堆成小山,妇孺们蜷缩在毯子底下,只露出一张张冻红的脸;右前景的路缘石上,一个小女孩独自站着,望着车队远去的方向。1945年1月13日,苏军发起东普鲁士攻势,数百万德意志平民在隆冬里踏上了西逃的路。

这场逃亡的恐惧并非凭空而来:1944年10月东普鲁士内默斯多夫村的杀戮经宣传放大后,妇孺在冰雪里套车的场面成了整个东部的日常。到2月,苏军已切断东普鲁士与德国本部的大部陆路,难民只能涌向波罗的海港口——从1月下旬起,德国海军发动『汉尼拔行动』,用军舰、货轮乃至渔船把近百万平民与数十万士兵经海路撤往西方,是史上规模最大的海上撤退。但泽在被围数周后于3月30日陷落,照片里的车队,只是那场大混乱里普通的一帧。
战后,奥得河-尼斯河以东的德意志人被整体迁出:1945到1949年间,总数一千二百余万人从东欧各地被驱逐或逃亡,是欧洲史上规模最大的强迫人口迁移之一;但泽从此是波兰的格但斯克。赫贝尔的这批照片由联邦档案馆完整保存——不拍士兵、只拍平民与街道的视角,让这帧画面成了东部大逃亡最沉静也最日常的记录之一。

en.title: Refugee Column at Danzig
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 146-1996-028-36A; photographer Brigitte Höber, taken on 20–21 February 1945 on the outskirts of Danzig (today Gdańsk).
en.points: Looked down on from above the street: a two-horse farm wagon loaded with bedding, baskets, women and children moves along the road, the people on it huddled under blankets; in the right foreground a small girl stands alone at the kerb.
story: Around 20 February 1945, the outskirts of Danzig: from a high point at the roadside the photographer Brigitte Höber looked down and shot this westbound refugee column — two draft horses pull a farm wagon on which bedding, baskets, sheaves and pots are heaped into a hill, the women and children huddled beneath blankets with only frost-reddened faces showing; on the kerbstone in the right foreground a small girl stands alone, looking after the column. On 13 January 1945 the Soviet army had opened its East Prussian offensive, and millions of German civilians set out westward in the depths of winter.

The fear behind the flight had a history: after the killing at the East Prussian village of Nemmersdorf in October 1944 was amplified by the propaganda, the sight of women and children harnessing carts in the ice and snow became the daily face of the whole east. By February the Soviet forces had cut most of the land routes between East Prussia and Germany proper, and the refugees pressed toward the Baltic ports — from late January the German navy ran Operation Hannibal, carrying nearly a million civilians and hundreds of thousands of soldiers westward by sea in warships, freighters and fishing boats alike, the largest seaborne evacuation in history. Danzig fell on 30 March after weeks of siege; the column in this photograph is one ordinary frame out of that vast disorder.

After the war the Germans east of the Oder and Neisse were expelled entire: between 1945 and 1949 more than twelve million people were driven out of or fled eastern Europe, one of the largest forced migrations in European history; Danzig became the Polish Gdańsk. Höber's photographs are preserved complete in the Federal Archives — a perspective that photographs no soldiers, only civilians and streets, and it makes this frame one of the stillest, most everyday records of the great flight from the east.

title: 骡队饮水
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏（Bild 183-B27180），国防军战地记者拉赫曼摄于1942年7月，苏联前线。画面要点：东欧村庄的土路上，一名意军士兵牵着驮满行装的骡子迎面走来，身后是绵延的骡队与随行士兵，背景是木屋与洋葱顶教堂的村舍天际线。
story: 这张照片藏于德国联邦档案馆，是国防军宣传连随军记者拉赫曼1942年7月在苏联前线拍下的战地报道，原始说明写着：『苏联前线，意大利人的骡队正被牵去饮水。』画面里，一名意大利士兵牵着头骡迎面走来，骡背上捆着卷起的行装与弹药箱，身后长长的骡队踏起尘土，一直排到村口的木屋与教堂脚下。牲口与人都低着头，只有摄影师的位置抬高了一点，把这支队伍的长度全收进了画面。

1942年7月，墨索里尼把驻苏的意大利远征军扩编为第八集团军，也就是『意大利驻俄集团军』（ARMIR），由加里波尔迪上将指挥，总兵力达二十三万余人，编成内有步兵军与三个阿尔卑斯山地师。这个半机械化的时代里，意军的运输却仍靠牲口：全军配属的骡马驮兽多达两万五千头，山地师甚至按『四名山地兵一头骡』的标准配属。8月13日，意军在顿河右岸接防了长达270公里的正面，为德军掩护斯大林格勒方向的侧翼。骡队就是这条漫长战线的命脉：弹药、口粮、木柴、伤员，全靠这些牲口沿着被雨水和车辙碾烂的土路来回搬运。
照片拍下的1942年7月，正是这支军队向前开进的顶峰——谁也想不到，五个月后它会被完全摧毁。1942年12月16日，苏军以四十余万兵力在顿河一线发起冬季攻势，意军防线两日内即被洞穿；1943年1月，被合围的阿尔卑斯军在尼古拉耶夫卡突围，朱利亚师带着四千头骡子出征，辗转回到意大利时只剩四十头。三十万东征的意大利士兵里，约有十一万人没能回来。这张骡队饮水的照片，定格的是那条不归路起点处的平静午后。

en.title: Watering the Mules
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 183-B27180; Wehrmacht war correspondent Lachmann, taken in July 1942 on the Soviet front.
en.points: On a dirt road through an East European village an Italian soldier leads a mule loaded with kit toward the camera; behind him the mule train and marching soldiers stretch away, with the skyline of wooden houses and an onion-domed church behind.
story: This photograph is held in the German Federal Archives, a battlefield report shot in July 1942 on the Soviet front by Lachmann, a correspondent with a Wehrmacht propaganda company; the original caption reads: Soviet front — an Italian mule train being led to water. In the frame an Italian soldier leads the point mule toward the camera, rolled kit and ammunition boxes lashed to its back, and the long train behind raises the dust all the way to the wooden houses and the church at the village edge. The animals and the men keep their heads down alike; only the photographer's slightly raised standpoint gathers the column's whole length into the picture.

In July 1942 Mussolini raised the Italian expeditionary corps in Russia into the Eighth Army — the Italian Army in Russia, ARMIR — under General Gariboldi, more than 230,000 men strong, with infantry corps and three Alpine mountain divisions. In this half-mechanised age, Italian transport still ran on animals: the army counted as many as 25,000 mules and horses, and the mountain divisions were scaled to one mule for every four mountain troops. On 13 August the Italians took over a 270-kilometre stretch on the right bank of the Don, covering the flank of the German drive toward Stalingrad. The mule trains were the lifeline of that long line: ammunition, rations, firewood and the wounded all moved on these animals, back and forth along roads churned to mud by rain and wheels.

July 1942, when this photograph was taken, was the summit of that army's advance — no one imagined that five months later it would be destroyed. On 16 December 1942 the Soviet army opened its winter offensive on the Don with more than 400,000 men, and the Italian line was broken within two days; in January 1943 the encircled Alpine Corps fought its way out at Nikolayevka — the Julia Division set out with 4,000 mules, and when the remnants struggled back to Italy, forty were left. Of the three hundred thousand Italian soldiers who marched east, some one hundred and ten thousand never came home. This photograph of mules on their way to water freezes a quiet afternoon at the starting point of a road with no return.

title: 沙漠行军
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏（Bild 101I-783-0104-09），国防军战地记者莫斯米勒（『非洲』宣传连）摄于1941年4月，北非。画面要点：沙漠公路上一队意军步兵迎面行军，前景一名戴钢盔、怀抱卡宾枪的士兵走在最前，身旁战友背着卷起的行装，左侧一辆SPA CL39卡车满载士兵随行，队伍延向地平线。
story: 这张照片藏于德国联邦档案馆，由随隆美尔非洲军行动的『非洲』宣传连记者莫斯米勒拍摄于1941年4月的北非：沙漠公路上，一队意大利步兵迎面走来——最前面的士兵戴钢盔、怀里抱着卡宾枪，身后的战友们背着卷起的毛毯与行装，水壶和饭盒挂在胸前；画面左侧，一辆意军标准SPA CL39卡车满载着士兵与器材随行，队伍一直排到地平线。人与车碾起的细尘悬在干热的空气里，没有遮天蔽日的沙暴，只有一眼望不到头的砾石滩。

1941年2月，隆美尔率德国非洲军抵达的黎波里，与意大利第10集团军合兵一处；3月底，德意联军从阿盖拉发起反攻，4月初克班加西，4月中旬围住托布鲁克、前出至埃及边境的塞卢姆——两个月里推进了上千公里。意军的阿里埃特装甲师、特兰托摩托化师与几个步兵师参加了这场攻势，承担了大量徒步与驮运勤务：非洲的战斗纵然以机械化闻名，真正把补给、弹药和士兵送过每一公里沙漠的，仍是照片里这样的双脚与卡车。这张照片拍下的4月，正是联军在滨海公路上东进的顶点。
半年后，战局在阿莱曼反转；再过一年多，突尼斯的意德军队于1943年5月集体投降，北非的战争以轴心国全军覆没告终。这张行军照没有炮火，却拍下了北非意军最真实的日常：公路、尘土、行装，以及无穷无尽的烈日下的路。

en.title: Desert March
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 101I-783-0104-09; Wehrmacht war correspondent Mossmiller of the Afrika propaganda company, taken in April 1941 in North Africa.
en.points: Along a desert road a column of Italian infantry marches toward the camera; at the front a helmeted soldier with a carbine cradled in his arms, the comrades behind him carrying rolled kit; on the left an SPA CL39 truck full of soldiers moves with the column, which runs on to the horizon.
story: This photograph is held in the German Federal Archives, taken in North Africa in April 1941 by Mossmiller of the Afrika propaganda company travelling with Rommel's Africa Corps: on a desert road a column of Italian infantry comes toward the camera — the man at the head in a helmet, a carbine cradled in his arms; the comrades behind with rolled blankets and kit on their backs, canteens and mess tins hung at their chests; on the left of the frame an SPA CL39, the Italian army's standard truck, carries soldiers and gear along with the column as it runs out to the horizon. The fine dust lifted by men and machines hangs in the dry heat; there is no sky-blackening sandstorm, only gravel flats without end.

In February 1941 Rommel brought the German Africa Corps to Tripoli and joined it to the Italian 10th Army; from the end of March the German-Italian force counterattacked out of El Agheila, took Benghazi in early April, and by mid-April had ringed Tobruk and pushed out to Sollum on the Egyptian frontier — more than a thousand kilometres in two months. The Italian Ariete armoured division, the Trento motorised division and several infantry divisions took part in that advance, carrying much of the work of marching and pack transport: the war in Africa was famous for its machines, but what actually moved supplies, ammunition and soldiers over every kilometre of desert were feet and trucks like those in this photograph. April, when it was taken, was the high point of the advance eastward along the coast road.

Half a year later the tide turned at El Alamein; a year and more after that the Italian and German armies in Tunisia surrendered together in May 1943, and the war in Africa ended with the destruction of the Axis force entire. This march photograph holds no gunfire, yet it catches the truest daily round of the Italians in North Africa: the road, the dust, the kit, and the endless miles under a pitiless sun.

title: 西西里的白旗
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏（Bild 146-1977-160-12），摄影师不详的德方档案照，1943年，西西里，档案馆原始说明为『西西里1943，意军投向英国人』。画面要点：地中海灌木坡地上，一名意军士兵高举绑在树枝上的白布走在前面，身旁战友用绷带吊着手臂，身后数十名士兵举着手沿山坡陆续走下，远处腾着烟尘。
story: 这张照片藏于德国联邦档案馆，是1943年夏西西里战役期间流传到德方档案里的一帧：地中海内陆的灌木坡地上，一名意大利士兵把白布高高绑在一根树枝上举过头顶，走在队伍最前；他身旁的战友用三角巾吊着受伤的手臂；身后几十名士兵举着手，沿着被炮火犁过的山坡陆续走下来，远处升着炮击的烟尘。他们交出的方向是英军阵地——德方档案的原始说明毫不客气地记作『意军投向英国人』。

1943年7月9日深夜，盟军舰队顶着八级大风扑向西西里南岸，次日拂晓抢滩成功。守岛的意大利第六集团军约二十万人大多是本地召募的后备部队，装备老旧，空中支援近于零；与之并肩的德军只有约三万人，却掌握着主力装甲部队。战役第一个月里，意军成建制崩溃，约十三万七千名轴心国士兵被俘，其中绝大多数是意大利人。8月17日盟军进占墨西拿，西西里战役结束。照片里这支举着白旗下山的队伍，就是那个夏天意大利军队整体命运的缩影。
西西里的崩溃直接压垮了墨索里尼政权：战役打响半个月后，7月25日，他被国王废黜拘禁；9月3日，巴多利奥政府与盟军签署停战协定，9月8日公开宣布，10月13日意大利对德宣战，成为『共同交战国』。照片里那些放下武器的士兵没能全部回家：数十万人被运往德国的战俘营，在异国的工矿区熬过剩下的战争岁月。

en.title: White Flags in Sicily
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 146-1977-160-12; German archival photograph, photographer unknown, 1943, Sicily; the archive's original caption reads: Sicily 1943, Italians surrendering to the British.
en.points: On a slope of Mediterranean scrub an Italian soldier walks in front holding a white cloth bound to a branch high over his head; beside him a comrade carries his arm in a sling, and behind, dozens of soldiers come down the slope in file with raised hands while smoke and dust rise in the distance.
story: This photograph is held in the German Federal Archives, one frame from the Sicilian campaign of summer 1943 that passed into the German files: on a slope of inland Mediterranean scrub an Italian soldier walks at the head of the column holding a white cloth tied to a branch high above his head; the comrade beside him carries a wounded arm slung in a triangular bandage; behind them dozens of soldiers come down the shell-ploughed slope one after another with their hands up, and the smoke of the shellfire hangs in the distance. The line they are giving themselves up to is British — and the German file's original caption sets it down without ceremony: Italians surrendering to the British.

Late on 9 July 1943 the Allied fleet ran through a near-gale against the south coast of Sicily and put its assault ashore at dawn the next day. The Italian Sixth Army holding the island, some 200,000 men, was mostly locally raised reserve formations with old equipment and close to no air support; the Germans alongside them fielded only some 30,000 men but held the main armoured force. Within the first month of the campaign the Italian army collapsed as formed units, and about 137,000 Axis soldiers went into captivity, the great majority of them Italians. On 17 August the Allies entered Messina, and the campaign ended. The column coming down this slope under white flags was the whole fate of the Italian army that summer in one picture.

The collapse in Sicily broke Mussolini's regime outright: half a month into the campaign, on 25 July, the king dismissed and imprisoned him; on 3 September the Badoglio government signed the armistice with the Allies, announced openly on 8 September, and on 13 October Italy declared war on Germany and became a co-belligerent. The soldiers laying down their arms in this photograph were not all to go home: hundreds of thousands were shipped to the prisoner-of-war camps of Germany and worked out the remaining war years in the mines and factory districts of a foreign country.

title: 海岸机枪阵地
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏（Bild 101I-316-1196-27），国防军战地记者德默（宣传连699）摄于1944年，意大利。画面要点：海岬下的滩头工事里，四名戴意大利钢盔的士兵背对镜头伏在石垒后，重机枪架在阵地正中指向海面，远处是平静的海湾与丘陵。
story: 这张照片藏于德国联邦档案馆，由国防军宣传连记者德默拍摄于1944年的意大利海岸：海岬投下的阴影里，四名戴着意大利M33钢盔的士兵伏在石块与沙袋垒成的机枪工事里，全部背对镜头，视线与枪口一同指向开阔的海面。重机枪的三脚架支在阵地正中，弹链已经上膛；远处的海湾风平浪静，海岸线上有白色的小镇与丘陵。照片没有记录交火，只有等待——这个阵地摆明了一件事：盟军若从这里登陆，第一梭子弹将从这里打出去。

1944年的意大利战线正一寸寸向北碾过亚平宁半岛：1月盟军在古斯塔夫防线前苦战并开辟安齐奥滩头，6月4日进入罗马，8月又在哥特防线前停了下来。就在陆军沿半岛纵轴拉锯的同时，漫长的海岸线仍是轴心国的心病——盟军的两栖登陆已经在萨莱诺与安齐奥证明过它的威胁，任何一段海滩都可能变成下一个战场。在北方的意大利社会共和国治下，仍有一批意大利官兵与德军并肩守备这些滩头阵地，用的还是意军自己的钢盔与布雷达机枪。照片里这组机枪手，守的就是这样一段无人来犯的海岸。
战争的最后一年，意大利战线的僵局直到1945年4月才被打破：盟军突破哥特防线向南急进，德军与意大利社会共和国的部队全线崩溃，5月2日在卡西比尔的投降书生效。照片里这片安静的海湾，便成了那场战争在半岛上最后的注脚之一。

en.title: Coastal Machine-Gun Post
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 101I-316-1196-27; Wehrmacht war correspondent Demmer of Propaganda Company 699, taken in 1944 in Italy.
en.points: In a beach position under a headland, four soldiers in Italian helmets crouch with their backs to the camera behind a parapet of stones; a heavy machine gun stands on its mount at the centre of the position, trained out over the water; beyond lies a calm bay with hills.
story: This photograph is held in the German Federal Archives, taken on the Italian coast in 1944 by Demmer, a correspondent of a Wehrmacht propaganda company: in the shadow thrown by a headland, four soldiers in Italian M33 helmets crouch in a machine-gun position built of stones and sandbags, all with their backs to the camera, their eyes and the gun's muzzle alike on the open sea. The heavy machine gun stands on its tripod at the centre of the position with the belt already in the breech; the bay beyond lies calm, white towns and hills along the shore. The photograph records no exchange of fire, only waiting — and the position says one thing plainly: if the Allies came ashore here, the first burst would leave from this gun.

Through 1944 the Italian front ground its way north up the Apennine peninsula: in January the Allies fought before the Gustav Line and opened the Anzio beachhead; on 4 June they entered Rome; by August they had stopped once more before the Gothic Line. While the armies sawed back and forth along the spine of the peninsula, the long coastline remained an Axis worry — the Allied amphibious landings at Salerno and Anzio had proved the threat, and any stretch of beach might open into the next battlefield. In the north, under the Italian Social Republic, Italian officers and soldiers still stood these beach positions alongside the Germans, with their own helmets and their own Breda machine guns. The machine-gun crew in this photograph held just such a coast — one that no one ever came to attack.

The deadlock on the Italian front held until April 1945: the Allies broke the Gothic Line and drove fast to the north, the German and Italian Social Republic forces collapsed along the whole line, and the surrender came into force on 2 May. This quiet bay became one of the war's last footnotes on the peninsula.

title: 登机出击
source: 意大利中央国家档案馆（ACS）二战照片档案库藏，摄影师不详，1943年3月19日，突尼斯马雷斯。画面要点：荒漠机场上，一名飞行员背着伞包攀进Macchi C.202战斗机的座舱，一名地勤站在翼下仰头照应，机身迷彩、白色识别带与尾翼白十字清晰，机号84-10。
story: 这张照片出自意大利中央国家档案馆的二战照片档案库，摄于1943年3月19日的突尼斯马雷斯前线：荒漠机场的碎石地上，一架Macchi C.202『霹雳』战斗机停在白色识别带漆成的机身前，一名飞行员背着降落伞包正攀进座舱，另一名地勤站在翼下仰头照应；机身上『84-10』的机号与尾翼的萨伏依白十字清晰可辨。次日，英军第八集团军对马雷斯防线的总攻——『拳击手行动』——正式打响。这张照片拍下的，正是大战前夜意大利空军的一次普通出击准备。

马雷斯防线是轴心国在突尼斯东南依托山脊与沼泽筑成的最后一道壁垒，守军是意德第1集团军——在北非的轴心国部队里，这支部队由意大利将军乔瓦尼·梅塞指挥。防线上的意大利步兵师顶住了英军首轮正面强攻，逼得蒙哥马利改用侧翼迂回；空中的情形却无法乐观：意大利皇家空军倾尽全力，能升空的C.202仍只有五十余架。『霹雳』是意大利战时最好的战斗机，缠斗敏捷、火力虽弱却胜任护航与拦截，第4联队等王牌部队用它打过马耳他、阿拉曼与突尼斯的每一场恶仗。
马雷斯在3月底失守，轴心国部队退向瓦迪阿卡里特，又退向突尼斯城；5月13日，北非的意德军队约25万人集体放下武器——梅塞在最后关头晋升元帅，随即与部下一起进了战俘营。照片里这名攀进座舱的飞行员没能留下姓名，但他的姿态留了下来：座舱盖敞开、伞带压在肩上，一场注定失败的战役里，出发仍是每天要做的事。

en.title: Boarding for the Sortie
en.source: Second World War photographic archive of the Archivio Centrale dello Stato (Central State Archives), Rome; photographer unknown, 19 March 1943, Mareth, Tunisia.
en.points: On a desert airfield a pilot with his parachute pack climbs into the cockpit of a Macchi C.202 fighter while a ground-crew man stands under the wing, head tipped back to help him; the camouflage, the white identification band and the white cross on the tail are all clear, the aircraft number 84-10.
story: This photograph comes from the Second World War photographic archive of Italy's Central State Archives, taken at the Mareth front in Tunisia on 19 March 1943: on the gravel of a desert airfield stands a Macchi C.202 Folgore fighter with the white identification band painted round its fuselage; a pilot with his parachute pack on his back climbs into the cockpit while a ground-crew man stands beneath the wing, head tipped back to help; the number 84-10 on the fuselage and the white cross of Savoy on the tail are both plain to read. The next day the British Eighth Army opened its full assault on the Mareth Line — Operation Pugilist. What the photograph holds is an ordinary sortie preparation by the Italian air force on the eve of that battle.

The Mareth Line was the last wall the Axis built in south-eastern Tunisia along ridge and marsh; its defenders were the Italian-German 1st Army — of the Axis forces in North Africa, the one commanded by the Italian general Giovanni Messe. The Italian infantry divisions on the line held the first frontal assault and forced Montgomery onto a flanking sweep; in the air the picture allowed no optimism: the whole strength of the Royal Italian Air Force still put up no more than some fifty C.202s. The Folgore — the lightning — was the best Italian fighter of the war, agile in the dogfight, lightly armed but equal to escort and interception; the 4th Wing and the other leading units flew it through every hard fight over Malta, at El Alamein and in Tunisia.

Mareth fell at the end of March; the Axis forces fell back on Wadi Akarit and then toward Tunis; on 13 May the Italian and German armies in North Africa, some 250,000 men, laid down their arms together — Messe was promoted marshal at the last hour and went with his soldiers into captivity. The pilot climbing into his cockpit in this photograph left no name behind, but his posture survives: canopy open, parachute straps across the shoulders — in a campaign already destined to be lost, taking off was still the day's work.

title: 那不勒斯的十月
source: 英国陆军影像摄影队第2组加德斯通军士摄于1943年10月1日，那不勒斯圣乔瓦尼-阿-卡博纳拉街。画面要点：石铺长街两侧是巴洛克老楼，欢呼的人群涌满街面，赤脚的少年们跑在队伍最前，有人挥帽、有人鼓掌，一名士兵被围在人潮中央，街道尽头隐在薄雾里。
story: 这张照片由英国陆军影像摄影队第2组的加德斯通军士拍摄于1943年10月1日：那不勒斯老城圣乔瓦尼-阿-卡博纳拉街的石板路面上，全城的人涌了出来——赤脚的少年们笑着跑在人潮最前，穿工装的汉子挥着帽子，阳台与窗口挂满了人，一名盟军士兵被围在人海中央几乎看不见。这是盟军开进那不勒斯的第一个上午，整座城市像一口烧开的锅。

开进来得并不容易，更不是恩赐：这座城市自己先站了起来。9月8日停战宣布后，德军占领那不勒斯，征用民房、驱赶居民、计划炸毁港口与全城；9月27日，被逼到绝路的市民在没有任何统一组织的情况下自发起义，用猎枪、私藏的步枪和从德军手里夺来的武器在街巷里筑起街垒，整整打了四天，六百六十余名那不勒斯人倒在石板路上。9月30日，德军撤出这座没能炸毁、也没能压服的城市。10月1日上午9时30分，英军国王龙骑兵卫队的装甲巡逻车最先驶入市区，第82空降师的部队随后跟进——照片里被人群围住的那名士兵，就属于最先开进来的部队。
那不勒斯是二战中唯一被授予意大利金质军事勇敢勋章的城市，授勋词写道：她的人民『以无愧于先辈的勇气，用三天三夜的战斗赢得了自由』。这张入城第一天的照片，记录的正是那场起义换来的时刻：街道还是废墟间的街道，人心已经先解放了。

en.title: Naples in October
en.source: Sergeant Gedstone, No. 2 Section, British Army Film and Photographic Unit, taken on 1 October 1943 in the Via San Giovanni a Carbonara, Naples.
en.points: Down a long paved street of baroque old houses a cheering crowd fills the roadway; barefoot boys run at the head of the column, some wave hats, some clap, a soldier stands swallowed at the centre of the human tide, and the far end of the street fades into haze.
story: This photograph was taken on 1 October 1943 by Sergeant Gedstone of No. 2 Section, British Army Film and Photographic Unit: on the paving of the Via San Giovanni a Carbonara in old Naples the whole city has poured out — barefoot boys run laughing at the head of the tide, men in working clothes wave their hats, the balconies and windows are hung with people, and an Allied soldier stands at the centre of the crowd, almost invisible within it. It is the first morning of the Allied entry into Naples, and the whole city is like a pot brought to the boil.

That entry came hard, and it was no gift: the city had first risen by itself. After the armistice was announced on 8 September the Germans occupied Naples, requisitioned houses, drove out the inhabitants and laid plans to blow up the port and the city entire; on 27 September, pushed past endurance, the people rose without any unified command, building barricades in the lanes with shotguns, hidden rifles and weapons torn from the Germans, and fought for four whole days; more than six hundred and sixty Neapolitans fell on the paving stones. On 30 September the Germans withdrew from the city they had neither blown up nor broken. At 09:30 on 1 October the armoured cars of the British King's Dragoon Guards drove in first, followed by units of the U.S. 82nd Airborne Division — the soldier the crowd swarms round in this photograph belonged to those leading troops.

Naples is the only city of the Second World War to be awarded the Italian Gold Medal of Military Valour; the citation says that its people, with courage worthy of their forebears, won their freedom in three days and three nights of fighting. This photograph of the first day of entry records what that rising bought: the streets are still streets among ruins, but the heart of the city had been liberated already.

title: 阿尔巴尼亚的坦克兵
source: 德国联邦档案馆藏（Bild 101I-203-1686-30），国防军战地记者普齐比拉摄于1943年9月，阿尔巴尼亚。画面要点：山地公路边，两名戴皮质坦克帽的意军坦克兵坐在坦克尾部休整，居前者侧望镜头，远处是层叠的山峦、林木与卡车。
story: 这张照片藏于德国联邦档案馆，由国防军战地记者普齐比拉拍摄于1943年9月的阿尔巴尼亚：山地公路的急弯处，两名戴着皮质坦克帽的意大利坦克兵坐在战车的尾部歇脚，居中的一位侧过脸望向镜头，神情平静得近乎松弛；另一人捧着杯子，像在分一壶什么。他们身后是阿尔巴尼亚层叠的山峦与公路，卡车队停在弯道上。整个画面没有一丝火药味——而这正是它最令人不安的地方：拍下它的那个九月，这些士兵的战争被从头顶上整个掀翻了。

意大利自1939年4月起吞并阿尔巴尼亚，把它经营成巴尔干占领区的支点。到1943年9月8日停战宣布时，达尔马佐将军的第九集团军仍有六个师、约十万人驻在阿尔巴尼亚。停战的消息没等来任何明确命令，全军的指挥在几天内崩解：9月11日德军开进地拉那，东线集团军群司令罗西在司令部里被俘；达尔马佐选择了谈判，9月中旬下令所部交出武器。约九万名意大利士兵就这样被昔日的盟友解除了武装，塞进运牲口的火车押往德国的劳改营；约一万五千人逃散进山，其中数千人带着武器投奔了阿尔巴尼亚游击队，编成了以葛兰西命名的国际营，一直打到战争结束。也有拒绝放下武器的部队——『佩鲁贾』师且战且退到海岸，9月22日弹尽投降，奇米内洛将军与一百三十名军官随后被德军枪杀。
照片里这两名坦克兵坐在战车上的平静一幕，就落在这些命运的岔路口上：快门按下的时候，他们还不知道自己将成为战俘、逃兵，还是游击队员。阿尔巴尼亚的九月，是意大利军队整场战争里最仓皇的一个月，而这帧照片是它来临之前的最后安静。

en.title: Tank Men in Albania
en.source: German Federal Archives (Bundesarchiv), Bild 101I-203-1686-30; Wehrmacht war correspondent Przybilla, taken in September 1943 in Albania.
en.points: At the roadside in the mountains, two Italian tank men in leather tank helmets sit resting on the rear of their tank; the nearer one turns his face toward the camera, and beyond rise folded ranges, woods and parked trucks.
story: This photograph is held in the German Federal Archives, taken in Albania in September 1943 by Przybilla, a Wehrmacht war correspondent: at a hairpin of the mountain road, two Italian tank men in leather tank helmets sit resting on the back of their vehicle; the one nearer the camera turns his face to the lens, his expression calm almost to slackness; the other holds a cup, as if sharing out of a pot. Behind them lie Albania's folded ranges and road, trucks parked on the bend. There is no trace of powder smoke anywhere in the frame — and that is its most unsettling quality: in the September it was taken, these soldiers' war was torn away from over their heads.

Italy had annexed Albania in April 1939 and built it into the anchor of its occupation of the Balkans. When the armistice was announced on 8 September 1943, General Dalmazzo's Ninth Army still held six divisions and about 100,000 men in Albania. No clear order came with the armistice, and the army's command came apart within days: on 11 September German troops entered Tirana and General Rosi, commanding the East Army Group, was taken at his headquarters; Dalmazzo chose negotiation, and in mid-September ordered his forces to give up their arms. About ninety thousand Italian soldiers were disarmed by the ally of the day before, packed into cattle trucks and carried off to the labour camps of Germany; about fifteen thousand scattered into the mountains, several thousand of them carrying their weapons to the Albanian partisans, formed into a battalion named for Gramsci, and fought to the end of the war. There were units that refused to lay down their arms — the Perugia Division fought its way back to the coast and surrendered, out of ammunition, on 22 September; General Ciminale and 130 of his officers were shot by the Germans afterwards.

The calm of these two tank men sitting on their vehicle falls exactly across the forking of those fates: when the shutter fell they did not yet know whether they would become prisoners, fugitives or partisans. Albania in September was the most harried month of the Italian army's whole war, and this photograph is its last quiet hour before the change.

title: 拉文纳的授勋
source: 英国陆军影像摄影队第2组鲍曼军士摄于1945年2月4日，拉文纳加里波第广场。画面要点：一列刚刚受阅的游击队员持布伦轻机枪在广场上肃立，前排战士神情轻松，队列中亦有曾持枪作战的女游击队员，背景是拉文纳的石砌公共建筑。
story: 这张照片出自英国陆军官方战地影像档案，由影像摄影队第2组的鲍曼军士拍摄于1945年2月4日的拉文纳加里波第广场：一列游击队员在广场上肃立受阅，肩上端着布伦轻机枪，穿戴却是清一色的英军作战服——几个月前，他们还是不能暴露姓名的地下战士。前排的年轻人们神情轻松，有人带着笑意；队列里也有女游击队员，与男人们并肩端着同样的枪。当天，第八集团军司令麦克里里中将在广场上，把一枚金质军事勇敢勋章别在了一个人的胸前。

受勋者是阿里戈·博尔德里尼，拉文纳人，战地代号『布洛』，第28加里波第旅『马里奥·戈尔迪尼』的指挥官。1944年夏天，他把罗马涅的各路游击队拧成了一支能打野战的队伍；12月4日，正是他的人马为英军第八集团军带路，兵不血刃地解放了拉文纳，保住了这座古城满城的马赛克与壁画。这座被游击队自己解放的城市，成了意大利抵抗运动的一块金字招牌：第二十八旅被获准保留建制、换发英军装备，作为正规战斗部队编入第八集团军序列，一直打到战争结束——这在遍地解散缴械的游击队里是绝无仅有的待遇。
1945年2月4日的这次授勋，是抵抗运动的第一枚金质军事勇敢勋章，也是唯一一次由盟军将领亲手颁发。博尔德里尼战后连任六届众议员、又入参议院，2008年在拉文纳去世，葬礼上全城送行。照片里这支短暂的队列，记录的正是抵抗运动从地下走到阳光下的那一刻：枪还是那些枪，扛枪的人已经从『暴徒』变成了受勋的战士。

en.title: Decorated in Ravenna
en.source: Sergeant Bowman, No. 2 Section, British Army Film and Photographic Unit, taken on 4 February 1945 in the Piazza Garibaldi, Ravenna.
en.points: A file of partisans just paraded stands in order in the square with Bren light machine guns; the men in the front rank look at ease, women partisans who had fought with the same arms stand in the file, and the stone public buildings of Ravenna rise behind.
story: This photograph comes from the British Army's official wartime film archive, taken in the Piazza Garibaldi at Ravenna on 4 February 1945 by Sergeant Bowman of No. 2 Film and Photographic Section: a file of partisans stands in review in the square, Bren light machine guns at their shoulders, dressed all alike in British battle dress — a few months before, they had been underground fighters whose names could not be spoken. The young men in the front rank look easy, some of them smiling; women partisans stand in the file shoulder to shoulder with the men, carrying the same guns. That day the commander of the Eighth Army, Lieutenant-General McCreery, pinned the Gold Medal of Military Valour to one man's chest in this square.

The man decorated was Arrigo Boldrini, born in Ravenna, field name Bulow, commander of the 28th Garibaldi Brigade Mario Gordini. Over the summer of 1944 he had welded the partisan bands of Romagna into a force that could fight in the open field; on 4 December it was his men who guided the British Eighth Army in to free Ravenna without a shot, keeping the city's mosaics and frescoes whole. A city liberated by its own partisans became a showcase of the Italian Resistance: the 28th Brigade was allowed to keep its organisation, was re-equipped by the British, and fought on as a formed combat formation within the order of battle of the Eighth Army until the end of the war — a treatment without parallel among the partisan bands everywhere else being disbanded and disarmed.

The decoration of 4 February 1945 was the first Gold Medal of Military Valour of the Resistance, and the only one ever presented by an Allied general in person. Boldrini afterwards sat six terms in the Chamber of Deputies and then in the Senate; he died in Ravenna in 2008, and the whole city walked behind his funeral. This brief file in the photograph records the moment the Resistance stepped out of the underground into the daylight: the guns were the same guns, but the men carrying them had gone from outlaws to decorated soldiers.

title: 出击珍珠港
source: 美国海军官方档案照片（编号 80-G-71198，现藏美国国家档案馆），摄于1941年12月7日清晨，中太平洋海上日军机动部队的航空母舰（一般认为是『翔鹤』号）飞行甲板。画面要点：高机位俯视，木质飞行甲板上一架九九式舰上爆击机正被几名甲板员推往待发位置，前景一架零式舰上战斗机旁围着作业人员，更远处还停着列成纵队的攻击机，甲板之外是翻涌着白浪的大海。
story: 1941年12月8日（东京时间）凌晨，南云忠一中将指挥的第一航空舰队抵达瓦胡岛以北约370公里的洋面，六艘航空母舰先后放飞两波共约350架飞机，扑向珍珠港的美国太平洋舰队。这张照片拍下的正是第二攻击队出击前的甲板：零式舰上战斗机停在前景，甲板员们把九九式舰上爆击机一架架推到起飞线上，木质甲板在工作人员脚下微微震颤。第一波飞机飞走之后，第二波紧接着发动，两波之间，机务人员几乎不曾停手。

攻击达成了战术上的完胜：美国太平洋舰队的战列舰部队被瘫痪，『亚利桑那』号弹药库爆炸坐沉，『俄克拉何马』号倾覆，美军共阵亡2400余人，188架飞机在地面上被击毁。但日本付出的代价同样深远——此战日军仅损失29架飞机和5艘袖珍潜艇，却有64名官兵再没有回来，其中55名是飞行队员，还包括9名袖珍潜艇乘员；而这批宝贵的老练飞行队，将在随后半年的消耗战中流尽。照片里这批整装待发的飞行员与飞机，正是那支开战即巅峰、此后再难补充的部队的留影。
原照随日军部队流落到北太平洋的阿图岛，1943年5月美军收复该岛时被缴获，后编入美国海军档案，编号80-G-71198，美国海军历史与遗产司令部注明『拍摄母舰据称是翔鹤』。翔鹤号在此后的珊瑚海、圣克鲁兹诸海战中屡建功勋，1944年6月19日在马里亚纳海战中被美军潜艇『棘鳍』号击沉——这张阿图岛缴获的甲板留影，成了它开战那天早晨为数不多的影像之一。

en.title: Taking Off for Pearl Harbor
en.source: Official U.S. Navy archival photograph (No. 80-G-71198, held at the U.S. National Archives), taken on the morning of 7 December 1941 on the flight deck of a carrier of the Japanese Mobile Force at sea in the Central Pacific (generally identified as the Shokaku).
en.points: Seen from a high angle, a Type 99 carrier bomber is being pushed toward its take-off position by deck crews on the wooden flight deck; a Type 0 carrier fighter stands in the foreground with maintenance men around it, attack aircraft are parked in column farther aft, and beyond the deck lies the open sea streaked with whitecaps.
story: In the early hours of 8 December 1941 Tokyo time, the First Air Fleet commanded by Vice Admiral Chuichi Nagumo reached waters some 370 kilometers north of Oahu, and its six carriers launched two waves totalling about 350 aircraft against the U.S. Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor. This photograph shows the deck before the second attack wave went off: Type 0 carrier fighters stand in the foreground while deck crews manhandle Type 99 carrier bombers one by one to the take-off line, the wooden deck trembling underfoot. Once the first wave had departed the second followed almost at once, and between the two the maintenance crews scarcely paused.

The attack was a complete tactical success: the Pacific Fleet's battleship force was paralyzed, the Arizona settled to the bottom after her magazine exploded, the Oklahoma capsized, more than 2,400 Americans were killed and 188 aircraft destroyed on the ground. Yet Japan's own price was equally far-reaching — the fleet lost only 29 aircraft and 5 midget submarines, but 64 officers and men never came back, 55 of them aircrew and 9 midget-submarine crewmen; and those precious, highly trained air groups would bleed away in the war of attrition of the following six months. The pilots and aircraft marshalling on this deck are the portrait of a force at its peak on the very first day of the war, one that could never be replaced.

The original print drifted with Japanese forces to Attu in the North Pacific, was captured when American troops retook the island in May 1943, and was later catalogued into the U.S. Navy archives as 80-G-71198; the Naval History and Heritage Command notes that the ship from which the photograph was taken is reportedly the Shokaku. Shokaku went on to distinguished service at Coral Sea and Santa Cruz and was sunk by the U.S. submarine Cavalla on 19 June 1944 during the Battle of the Philippine Sea — this deck scene captured on Attu remains one of the few images of her on the morning the war began.

title: 樱花待发
source: 美国海军官方照片（美国海军航空博物馆藏，编号 1996.488.161.017），摄于1945年，日本本土的海军特攻基地。画面要点：停机坪上一架挂载『樱花』一一型人操火箭弹的一式陆上攻击机二四型丙停在画面上部，九名待命机组身穿飞行服、头戴飞行帽围坐在前景的地面上休息交谈。
story: 画面里那架双引擎轰炸机腹下挂着的短粗小飞机，是海军『樱花』一一型——木制机翼、火箭推进、弹头装药的有人滑翔弹，由改装的一式陆上攻击机（二四型丙，即 G4M2e）驮着飞向目标后脱离俯冲。操作它的是第七二一海军航空队，绰号『神雷部队』。1945年3月21日，五十五架樱花母机在数十架零战护卫下从鹿屋基地出击冲绳以东海面，却在距离美军舰队尚远之处被舰载机拦截，母机被迫提前投放或带弹返航，几乎全军覆没——樱花战的第一次出击就这样黯然收场。
此后樱花改以小规模零散出击，配合常规特攻机行动。它速度快、俯冲猛，曾于1945年4月12日击沉雷达哨驱逐舰『阿贝利』号——这是整场战争中樱花取得的唯一确定战果，其余出击大多被拦截于途中。驮樱花的母机笨重缓慢，是最容易被击落的机型之一；每出动一架樱花，就意味着母机乘员与樱花驾驶员两组人马一起踏上不归途。照片中围坐在母机前休息的这队待命机组，正处在出击命令下达之前的空白时间里。
这张照片由美军在战后收入官方档案，现藏佛罗里达州彭萨科拉的美国国家海军航空博物馆。画面里没有出击的悲壮，只有一群年轻飞行员坐在平整过的场地上说话，身后那架挂着樱花的母机安静地停着——特攻战术把这样的日常与死亡直接叠在一起，这正是它留给后世影像里最不安的地方。

en.title: Ohka Crews on Standby
en.source: Official U.S. Navy photograph (National Naval Aviation Museum, accession 1996.488.161.017), taken in 1945 at a naval special-attack base in the Japanese home islands.
en.points: On the hardstand in the upper part of the frame stands a Type 1 land attack bomber Model 24C with an Ohka Model 11 manned rocket bomb slung beneath its fuselage; nine crewmen on standby, in flight suits and flying caps, sit on the ground in the foreground, resting and talking.
story: The stubby little aircraft slung beneath the twin-engine bomber is the navy's Ohka Model 11 — a manned glide bomb with wooden wings, rocket propulsion and an explosive warhead, carried toward the target by a converted Type 1 land attack bomber (Model 24C, the G4M2e) and released to dive. The unit that operated it was the 721st Naval Air Group, nicknamed the Jinrai ('Divine Thunder') unit. On 21 March 1945, fifty-five Ohka mother planes sortied from Kanoya toward the waters east of Okinawa under escort by dozens of Zero fighters, but were intercepted by carrier aircraft well short of the American fleet; the bombers were forced to release their Ohkas early or turn back with them still aboard, and the force was all but annihilated — the first Ohka mission ended in dismal failure.

Afterwards the Ohka was committed in small, scattered sorties alongside conventional special-attack aircraft. Fast and violent in its dive, it sank the radar-picket destroyer USS Mannert L. Abele on 12 April 1945 — the only confirmed Ohka success of the entire war; most other sorties were intercepted en route. The mother plane that carried it was heavy and slow, one of the easiest aircraft of all to shoot down, and every Ohka launch meant two crews setting out on a one-way mission at once — the bomber's crew and the Ohka pilot. The standby crews resting in front of the mother plane in this photograph sit in the empty interval before the order to sortie comes down.

This photograph entered the official U.S. Navy archives after the war and is now held at the National Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola, Florida. There is nothing of heroic departure in the frame — only a group of young pilots sitting on the graded ground, talking, with the Ohka-carrying mother plane parked quietly behind them. The special-attack tactic laid such ordinariness directly on top of death, and that is the most unsettling thing about the images it left to posterity.

title: 银座空袭
source: 菊池俊吉摄于1945年1月27日午后，东京银座四丁目。当天约七十架 B-29 在白昼对东京都心繁华街进行了首次大规模空袭。画面要点：街口一座建筑正从窗口喷出烈焰，消防队员拉着水龙带向火点射水，街面行人奔走避难，前景烧焦的树枝与倾侧的电线杆横过画面。
story: 1945年1月27日下午，七十架左右的 B-29 首次把炸弹投在了东京最繁华的地段：银座、有乐町、京桥、丸之内一带燃起大火，五百三十余人丧生。此前的空袭目标多为城郊军需工厂，这一天的白昼轰炸宣告：东京的市中心再无安全可言。照片拍下的正是空袭当日的银座四丁目——临街建筑从窗洞里喷出火焰，消防队的水柱向着火点倾泻，行人沿街面奔走，冬天的行道树只剩下焦黑的枯枝。
按下快门的菊池俊吉是日本战灾记录摄影的代表人物。他从1942年杜立特空袭后便开始拍摄空袭后的东京，此后每一次大空袭都赶到现场，留下了规模庞大的战灾底片，东京都写真美术馆至今藏有他题名《空袭（银座）》的作品。在当时的出版管制下，这些记录多数要等到战后才得以面世，它们后来成为复原东京空袭现场最可靠的一手影像。
这次空袭只是开始。两个多月后的3月10日凌晨，三百余架 B-29 把下町一带烧成白地，5月下旬的连续夜袭又烧掉山手的大片街区，银座四丁目那座著名的和光钟楼周边尽成瓦砾。这张1月27日的照片记录的，是『繁华街也会燃烧』这个事实第一次被影像固定的时刻。

en.title: The Ginza Air Raid
en.source: Photographed by Toshikichi Kikuchi on the afternoon of 27 January 1945 at Ginza 4-chome, Tokyo. That day some seventy B-29s carried out the first large-scale daylight raid on the central shopping districts of Tokyo.
en.points: At a street corner a building is spouting flame from its windows as firemen haul hoses toward the fire and play water on it; pedestrians run for shelter along the street, and in the foreground charred branches and a leaning utility pole cross the frame.
story: On the afternoon of 27 January 1945, some seventy B-29s dropped their bombs on Tokyo's most fashionable districts for the first time: fire broke out across Ginza, Yurakucho, Kyobashi and Marunouchi, and more than 530 people were killed. Earlier raids had mostly targeted suburban munitions plants; this daylight bombardment announced that the city's heart was no longer safe. The photograph was taken that same day at Ginza 4-chome — street-front buildings pouring flame from their window openings, arcs of firemen's water falling on the fire, pedestrians running along the street, and the winter roadside trees reduced to blackened bare branches.

Toshikichi Kikuchi, who pressed the shutter, is a leading figure of Japanese war-damage photography. He began photographing Tokyo after air raids from the time of the Doolittle Raid in 1942, went to the scene of every major raid that followed, and left behind an enormous body of war-damage negatives; the Tokyo Photographic Art Museum still holds his work titled 'Air Raid (Ginza)'. Under the censorship of the day most of these records could not be published until after the war, and they have since become the most reliable first-hand images for reconstructing the Tokyo air raids.

This raid was only the beginning. In the small hours of 10 March, two months later, more than three hundred B-29s burned the downtown Shitamachi districts to bare ground; the successive night raids of late May destroyed large stretches of Yamanote; and the area around the famous Wako clock tower at Ginza 4-chome was reduced to rubble. What this photograph of 27 January fixed on film, for the first time, was the fact that the fashionable streets too could burn.

title: 焦土板车
source: 石川光陽摄于1945年3月，东京大空袭后的市街。画面要点：一名男子肩勒车辕，拉着堆满被褥与家什的荷车快步穿过瓦砾，身旁跟着年幼的孩子，四周是烧塌的木屋残骸，路边立着烧剩的石造墓塔与残破的日文招牌，前景是电车轨道。
story: 1945年3月10日凌晨，三百余架 B-29 依着西北风低空掠过东京下町，在两个多小时里投下约五十万枚 M69 凝固汽油弹。江东、墨田、台东一带的木造街区烧成一片白地，四十一平方公里的市区一夜间消失，死者约十万，是战争史上单一空袭造成死亡人数最高的一夜。天亮之后，幸存者做的第一件事，就是从灰烬里抢出没烧掉的家当——照片里那辆堆满被褥、衣箱与锅釜的荷车，正是这场大迁徙的一个缩影。
按快门的石川光陽是高知新闻社东京支局的摄影记者。3月10日清晨，他骑车赶进尚未熄火的火场，在余烬未冷的街巷里拍下大量现场照片，是留下3月10日当日市街影像最多的摄影师之一。他拍摄的被难者、废墟与迁徙队伍，战后多次以写真展与图录的形式公开，成为东京大空袭记忆里最重要的私人记录之一。
照片里的墓地石塔与医院招牌还立在原处，轨道从瓦砾间穿过——城市失去了街区，却还认得出原来的骨架。3月10日之后轰炸没有停：5月25日与26日的夜袭又烧掉山手的大片住宅区，数百万人从东京逃散。这张照片里的荷车，就这样从一个街区推向下一个街区，推在整个战败之年最前方。

en.title: Handcart Through the Scorched Earth
en.source: Photographed by Koyo Ishikawa in March 1945, on the streets of Tokyo after the great air raid.
